embody-lab-somatic-psychedelic.name: Somatic Psychedelic Facilitator Certificate
embody-lab-somatic-psychedelic.one_line: A $1,047 self-paced online certificate that teaches somatic and harm-reduction skills for preparation, sitting and integration — open to anyone, licensed or not, and it changes no one's scope of practice.
summary: This is a 50-hour, entirely online, entirely on-demand certificate. There is no cohort, no start date, no application and no admissions screening — you buy it and get lifetime access to a video library. Three modules of 12 hours each (Preparation, Facilitation Skills, Integration) plus pre-recorded extras and three hours of reflection and self-practice work. It is the cheapest and lowest-commitment thing in this directory by an order of magnitude, and it should be understood as a well-taught set of lectures rather than as training that qualifies you to do anything new.

The faculty list is genuinely strong and is most of what you are paying for: Bessel van der Kolk, Peter Levine, Gabor Maté, Richard Schwartz, Gül Dölen, Devon Christie, Atira Tan, Licia Sky, Chara Caruthers and Elder Duncan. Three further faculty — Rae Johnson, Scott Lyons and 'Michaela' — are named as running live Q&A support sessions. The content genuinely does what the title says: it maps somatic-psychology skills onto the three phases of a psychedelic session. Preparation covers screening tools, consent and containment, somatic intention-setting and resourcing. Facilitation covers a framework for supportive touch and touch alternatives, music, therapeutic ritual and cultural appropriation, transference and countertransference, rupture and repair, dosage and the psycholytic/psychedelic distinction, and risk mitigation. Integration covers a somatic integration model — normalising, regulation, meaning-making, metabolising, transpersonal support, action planning — plus practitioner self-care.

It is open to non-clinicians, and this matters more than the marketing suggests. The 'who this is for' list runs to twenty-odd categories including coaches, yoga teachers, massage therapists, meditation teachers, clergy, educators and 'other wellness professionals' alongside psychologists, social workers, physicians and nurses. The Embody Lab is explicit: the program 'caters to a diverse audience, including licensed therapists and unlicensed practitioners.' On completion it tells graduates the title they may use is 'Somatic Psychedelic Facilitator.' That title is not regulated, not protected and not recognised by any licensing board in California or anywhere else in the United States. A California LMFT taking this course should understand that they will hold the same certificate as a yoga teacher who took the same videos, and that the certificate confers nothing on either of them beyond the knowledge. What a licensed therapist has, and the yoga teacher does not, is a licence — and the licence is what governs what either of them may legally do.

Two practical cautions. First, the page you buy is titled for a 2025 cohort and reads like the archived version of what was once a live program: the FAQ says 'an orientation session was only provided for the live program,' 'scholarships were only available for the live program' and 'captioning was only available during the live sessions.' There is no separate 2026 cohort page — this product URL is the only Somatic Psychedelic Facilitator listing on The Embody Lab's site as of 6 August 2026. Second, the continuing-education claim needs reading twice. The program page says '50 hours — this program offers 50 hours of continuing education credits,' but the FAQ says the APA continuing education (48 hours, via co-sponsor Spiritual Competency Academy, which the California BBS accepts for LMFT, LCSW, LPCC and LEP renewal) applied to the live program and that '*Live* attendance was required.' If BBS-countable CE is why you are buying this, confirm in writing before you pay.

cost.note: $1,047 non-member, one-time payment. $894 for members; membership is being promoted at $10 for the first 30 days then $26/month, so a first-year member route works out cheaper than the non-member price. Payment plans offered at checkout (terms not published). No application fee. Registration Guarantee: full refund up to 48 hours before the course start date, no questions asked.

embody-lab-somatic-psychedelic.length: Self-paced with lifetime access. No fixed duration, no cohort, no registration deadline.
embody-lab-somatic-psychedelic.hours: 50 hours total: three modules of 12 hours each (36 hours), plus pre-recorded video content and 3 hours of reflection and self-practice work. Certificate completion additionally requires 10 hours of practice coaching sessions arranged outside class time, self-evaluation and reflection forms for each module, and a conversation with another student about the program.
embody-lab-somatic-psychedelic.format: Online, self-paced, on demand. All content sits in a content library available on registration, with downloadable video and audio, PDFs and English transcripts. Three live faculty Q&A support sessions (Rae Johnson, Scott Lyons and Michaela) are listed for 30 September, 15 October and 5 November, recorded and added to the library within 48 hours. An online community forum is included.
embody-lab-somatic-psychedelic.eligibility: Open to everyone. No licence, degree, prerequisite or admissions process. The site lists the intended audience as psychedelic facilitators, psychedelic support care workers, integration practitioners, social workers, mental health and pastoral counsellors, yoga therapists and yoga teachers, movement therapists, coaches, physicians (MD, DO, ND, DC), physician assistants, nurses and nurse practitioners, psychologists, emergency medical personnel, meditation teachers, educators, massage therapists, acupuncturists and body workers, hypnotherapists, kinesiologists, complementary and alternative medicine professionals, clergy and religious leaders, and other wellness professionals.

curriculum.detail: Part 1 theory: a theoretical orientation to somatic psychedelic-assisted therapies; core principles of somatic psychology; mindfulness/embodiment science and its intersection with psychedelic science; clinical versus ceremonial contexts; asynchronous reviews of psychedelic research history, drug classes (classical, empathogens, dissociatives, atypical), macro versus microdosing, traditional plant medicines and Indigenous histories, and mechanism theories (neurochemical, connectome/DMN). Ethics, duty of care and informed consent, framed around 'the enhanced and unique vulnerabilities of participants seeking psychedelic-assisted therapies.' Part 2 skills: five elements of preparation (creating a healing context/set and setting, psychoeducation, consent and agreements, somatic intention setting, somatic resourcing); building a screening approach using team-based care, a list of psychological flags and assessment of a participant's socio-environmental safety nets; working within an interdisciplinary team and within scope of practice; a preparation checklist.

Part 1 theory: overview of a psychedelic session; Kolb's experiential learning cycle applied to somatic psychedelic sessions; a framework for supportive touch and touch alternatives; principles for using music; therapeutic ritual with cultural safety and sensitivity, and avoiding cultural appropriation; trauma-informed language and the difference between reparative/corrective and retraumatising experiences; risk mitigation and safety strategies during the session; co-therapy and individual versus group facilitation; transference and countertransference, rupture and repair, and appropriate self-disclosure; dosage considerations across substances including the difference between psychedelic and psycholytic therapy; immediate post-session care. Part 2 skills: therapeutic presence, invitational embodied inquiry, interoceptive self-awareness, dual awareness and tracking, somatic communication, and using states of awareness to contain, protect and shape the space.

Part 1: post-session sensitivity, enhanced learning and neuroplasticity; assessing integration needs (normalising, metabolising, regulation, meaning-making, connection and community, transpersonal/spiritual needs, action planning); embodied integration via Kolb's cycle, bottom-up processing and somatic anchoring; steps for integration recovery and 'understanding a practitioner's scope of practice'; self-directed integration versus integration therapeutic support. Part 2: applying the steps of the Somatic Integration Model; supporting new patterns during the window of enhanced learning; therapist self-care practices.

3 hours of reflection and self-practice work; watching all program videos; self-evaluation and reflection forms per module; 10 hours of practice coaching sessions outside class times; a meaningful conversation with another student about the program; full payment.

can: Offer psychedelic integration work in California. This is the honest core use of the certificate. Integration is talking to a client about an experience they had somewhere else, and for a licensed therapist it is ordinary psychotherapy — no special credential required, and the somatic integration model taught here is directly usable.

Bring somatic, touch-framework and harm-reduction skills into ketamine-assisted psychotherapy, which is the only psychedelic modality a California therapist can currently practise. The therapist does not prescribe; a physician, NP or PA evaluates and prescribes, and the therapist does preparation, sitting and integration.
Use the material as harm-reduction and screening literacy — how to talk to clients who are already using psychedelics outside a clinical setting, what psychological flags to watch for, when to refer.

Possibly count it toward California BBS continuing education, but verify first. APA CE (48 hours) was offered through co-sponsor Spiritual Competency Academy, and the California BBS accepts APA-sponsor CE for LCSW, LPCC, LEP and LMFT renewal — but the FAQ states that live attendance was required for those CEs, while the program page advertises '50 hours of continuing education credits.' These two statements are not reconcilable from the page alone.
Use the title 'Somatic Psychedelic Facilitator,' which The Embody Lab explicitly grants. Understand that it is a marketing title, not a credential.
cannot: Change your licence or scope of practice. The California Board of Behavioral Sciences neither recognises nor requires this certificate, and holding it adds nothing to an LMFT, LCSW, LPCC or psychologist licence.

Legally administer, supply or sit with psilocybin, MDMA, LSD or ayahuasca for clients in California. Psilocybin and psilocyn are Schedule I under California Health & Safety Code §11054(d)(18)-(19); MDMA-assisted therapy has no FDA approval following the August 2024 complete response letter to Lykos Therapeutics, and no psychedelic other than ketamine is available to prescribe as of August 2026.

Qualify for the Oregon psilocybin facilitator licence. The Embody Lab does not appear on the Oregon Health Authority's list of training programs with approved curriculum (checked 6 August 2026, 15 programs listed).
Qualify for the Colorado natural medicine facilitator licence. The Embody Lab does not appear on Colorado DORA's list of approved Natural Medicine Training Programs (checked 6 August 2026).

Give an unlicensed graduate any legal ability to provide mental health treatment. A coach or yoga teacher who completes this certificate and then offers 'somatic psychedelic facilitation' involving a Schedule I substance is committing a crime and, if they present it as treatment, potentially unlicensed practice as well. The certificate does not insulate them and it does not insulate a licensed therapist who supervises or partners with them.
Substitute for supervised, hands-on training. The program says so itself.
Provide any live, in-person or experiential component. There is none. Everything is video.
scope.disclaimer_quote: Upon successful completion of our 50-hour certificate program in "Somatic Psychedelic Facilitation," participants will gain a foundational understanding of the intricate interplay between somatic psychology and psychedelic therapy. This program is not just a culmination but a beginning, marking the initiation of a lifelong learning journey. We emphasize the importance of ongoing mentorship, supervision, and peer consultation for continued growth in this evolving field. While the program provides a robust foundation, participants are responsible for navigating the regulatory and legal aspects of their care provision. We encourage practicing within a community framework, fostering collaboration and discouraging isolated practices. This program caters to a diverse audience, including licensed therapists and unlicensed practitioners; however, it is vital to recognize that completion of this program is not a final destination but a stepping stone, and ongoing effort and learning are essential for ethical and effective somatic psychedelic facilitation.

faculty: Bessel van der Kolk, MD — author of The Body Keeps the Score; the best-known name on the roster and the main draw for many buyers.
Peter Levine, PhD — originator of Somatic Experiencing.

Devon Christie, MD — clinician with hands-on MDMA and ketamine-assisted therapy trial experience; the most directly relevant practical voice on the list.
Atira Tan — trauma therapist and the lead voice on the somatic-psychedelic curriculum.
Licia Sky — somatic and embodied-movement educator, frequent collaborator of van der Kolk's.
Chara Caruthers — yoga therapist and somatic educator.
Elder Duncan, PhD — listed lead faculty.
Rae Johnson, Scott Lyons and 'Michaela' — named as the three faculty who run the live Q&A support sessions.

fluence-training.name: Fluence Professional Certificates (Psychedelic Harm Reduction and Integration Therapy; Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy; Psilocybin Facilitation)
fluence-training.org: Fluence (Fluence International, Inc.) — founded by Dr. Ingmar Gorman and Dr. Elizabeth Nielson
fluence-training.location: Live-online (US-based; registered in New York), with an in-person practicum in Denver, Colorado for the psilocybin pathway
fluence-training.one_line: The training built explicitly for licensed clinicians working inside current law: three certificate tracks at $5,500–$7,000, all requiring a psychotherapy licence, all APA-CE-bearing, and only one of which — the Colorado psilocybin pathway — leads to any state credential.
summary: Fluence was founded in 2019 by two psychologists who had actually run psychedelic trials: Elizabeth Nielson (psilocybin for alcohol use disorder at NYU; MAPS Phase 3 site co-PI; Compass Pathways Phase 2b at New York State Psychiatric Institute) and Ingmar Gorman. Its distinguishing commitment is a scope-of-practice discipline the rest of this field mostly lacks. Nielson, in a 2024 Psychedelic Alpha interview: 'We always want to be training people for things that they can do within their scope of practise, either as a licenced provider in the community or on a research study where there's an avenue to use that skill set. That's been one of our guiding principles since we started, which is why you won't see us offering training in modalities where there isn't a clear pathway to use.' That is the whole thesis, and it is why Fluence sells integration and ketamine training to Americans rather than MDMA facilitation.

The structure as of August 2026 is a two-step ladder. Everyone starts with Essentials of Psychedelic Therapy — 6 weeks, live-online, 22 CE hours, $2,195 for the autumn 2026 cohorts, and it ships with 12 hours of on-demand video from the Introduction to Psychedelic Therapy course. You then add one Specialty course to earn a Professional Certificate: Psychedelic Harm Reduction and Integration Therapy (PHRI) or Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy, each 12 weeks and 20 CE hours at $3,500 standalone, or the longer Psilocybin Facilitation track. Bundled, PHRI and KAP certificates are $5,500 (18 weeks, 42 CE hours) and Psilocybin Facilitation is $7,000 (28 weeks, 42 CE hours). Worth noting for a buyer: the site advertises 'Buy the Professional Certificate for a 20% discount!', but $2,195 + $3,500 = $5,695 against a $5,500 bundle price, which is a saving of $195, or about 3%. Payment plans exist (Fluence in-house instalments on some products, plus Affirm/PayPal at checkout) and there is a Diversity Fund you can apply to.

The 'integration' framing is the thing that separates Fluence from a facilitator school, and it is a legal distinction rather than a stylistic one. Psychedelic Harm Reduction and Integration Therapy is about supporting clients who are using psychedelics somewhere else — 'whether in a psychotherapy setting, alongside a ketamine clinic, or in the context of clients' independent, non-clinical use.' Nothing in it requires you to be present while anyone takes a drug, so, as Fluence puts it, 'it is applicable in any state.' Facilitator training, by contrast, prepares you to sit with someone during a dosing session, which is only lawful where a state has built a programme for it. Fluence separates these two things cleanly and tells you which is which — the honest version of a distinction many programmes blur.

For a California reader the practical map is short. The KAP certificate is the only track that changes what you can do at work on Monday, and even then it changes your competence, not your authority: you still need a prescribing partner. The PHRI certificate formalises integration work you are already permitted to do. The Psilocybin Facilitation certificate is a real state pathway — Fluence International, Inc. is listed on Colorado DORA's Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs register (didactic yes, practicum yes, consultation 'Available Late 2026') — but it is a Colorado credential. It does nothing in California, and Fluence does not currently appear on Oregon Psilocybin Services' list of active approved training programmes, which is consistent with its own advice: 'if you are primarily interested in practicing in Oregon, the most reliable current path is to pursue an Oregon-specific training.'

fluence-training.format: Live-online cohort classes with 'live roleplays for case-oriented learning', supported by on-demand video, a mobile app, and a peer community. The Psilocybin Facilitation track adds a mandatory in-person practicum in Denver hosted by a partner, the Psychedelic Research and Training Institute (PRATI). fluence-training.eligibility: 'Licensed Psychotherapist' is listed as the requirement on Essentials and on all three certificates. Fluence, verbatim: 'Fluence certificate programs are not a pathway to obtaining a psychotherapy license. They are continuing education and professional development programs designed for clinicians who are already licensed or credentialed in a relevant mental health field. In other words, you bring your license.' One documented exception: for PHRI, 'on a case-by-case basis, we also accept a limited number of professional coaches, credentialed counselors, and peer support providers into each course session' — by arrangement via info@fluencetraining.com. The KAP and Psilocybin Facilitation certificates state a valid licence is required for enrolment. Within the certificate ladder, Essentials is the prerequisite for every Specialty; Psilocybin Preparation and Integration precedes Natural Medicine Facilitation, which precedes the practicum (which additionally requires a Colorado training license). Non-clinicians are directed to the open-enrolment Introduction to Psychedelic Therapy instead.

curriculum.module: Course 01 — Essentials of Psychedelic Therapy (core, required for all three certificates)
curriculum.detail: 'This 6-week, live online Essentials course is the cornerstone of our professional certification programs... You will explore the core principles of psychedelic-assisted therapy and how it differs from harm reduction and integration approaches. The course covers key clinical concepts, preparation strategies, and supportive practices for working with clients before, during, and after psychedelic experiences. Throughout the program, emphasis is placed on applying these skills in a way that is ethical, responsible, and aligned with your scope of practice.' 22 CE hours; enrolment includes 12 hours of on-demand video from Introduction to Psychedelic Therapy. $2,195.

curriculum.module: Course 02 — Specialty: Psychedelic Harm Reduction and Integration Therapy (PHRI)
curriculum.detail: 12 weeks, 20 CE hours, $3,500 standalone. 'This 12-week course equips you with the knowledge and tools to work with patients who are using psychedelics in non-clinical settings. On completion of this course you will be able to safely and effectively support patients before and after psychedelic experiences.' The certificate overview adds: assessing readiness and motivation; classic psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD) and non-classic (ketamine, MDMA); preparation, set, setting, and dosing considerations; integration support; 'supporting long-term integration and translating PHRI into a legal, ethical practice.'

12 weeks, 20 CE hours, $3,500 standalone, 8 hours of on-demand video. 'This 12-week professional certification equips you with the knowledge and skills to deliver Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy... On completion of this course you will be able to safely and effectively support patients before, during and after ketamine experiences.' The certificate FAQ: 'This certificate program prepares clinicians to expand their knowledge and practice to include ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP). It offers comprehensive insights and practical skills essential for competent and ethical practice in KAP.'

curriculum.module: Psilocybin Facilitation — Course 02: Psilocybin Preparation and Integration
curriculum.detail: 12 weeks, 20 CE hours, $3,000 standalone. 'This course focuses on how psilocybin works—biologically and experientially—and how to support individuals preparing for and integrating their psilocybin experiences. You'll explore harm reduction principles, informed consent and screening, safe dosing guidelines, and integration methods.'

curriculum.module: Psilocybin Facilitation — Course 03: Natural Medicine Facilitation
curriculum.detail: 10 weeks (2 Saturdays, first and last week), $2,500 standalone. 'This course covers the essential aspects of psilocybin facilitation, including Colorado-specific requirements, group facilitation techniques, facilitator self-care, and guidelines for ethical boundaries and therapeutic touch.' Fluence: 'At this stage you can receive your training license from Colorado.'

curriculum.module: Psilocybin Facilitation — Course 04: Psilocybin Practicum (with PRATI)
curriculum.detail: 4-day in-person practicum in Denver. 'Put your knowledge into practice with a practicum hosted by top training partners, meeting Colorado guidelines to safely facilitate and observe non-ordinary states of consciousness.' 'Our training partner, Psychedelic Research and Training Institute (PRATI), has been carefully selected as the top training provider in the industry.' Requires a Colorado training license. Listed at $0 in Fluence's own catalogue, which suggests it is booked and paid through PRATI rather than Fluence.

curriculum.module: Psilocybin Facilitation — Final step: post-licensure consultation
curriculum.detail: 'Colorado regulations require 40 additional hours of consultation to obtain your full license.' Fluence's own Colorado listing shows consultation as 'Available Late 2026', so as of August 2026 you would need to source those hours elsewhere.

curriculum.module: Introduction to Ketamine-Assisted Therapy (on-demand entry point)
curriculum.detail: 8 hours on-demand, 8 CE hours, $395. Four sections: Foundations (clinical, pharmacological, ethical and research context); Preparation (screening, consent, set and setting, expectations, intentions, resourcing); Administration (dosing session structure and facilitation, supporting challenging experiences); Integration. Fluence's own caveat, verbatim: 'This is educational content designed to provide background knowledge and clinical orientation. It is not, on its own, clinical skills training.'

curriculum.module: Introduction to Psychedelic Therapy (open to non-clinicians)
curriculum.detail: 12 hours on-demand, $295 (a $89 promo variant also listed). Covers molecule-specific education (MDMA, psilocybin, ketamine), best practices for harm reduction and integration therapy, and psychedelic practice fundamentals. This is the track Fluence points people to if they are not a licensed psychotherapist.

Priced individually and sold on-demand or live: Applied Mindfulness for Psychedelic Therapists $250; Ayahuasca: The Basics for Therapists $75; Foundations of Ibogaine $25; DMT Research for Clinicians $25; Trauma-Informed Psychedelic Therapy $25; Introduction to MDMA-Assisted Therapy Research $25; Introduction to Ketamine for Mental Health $125; Clinical Site Toolkit $295; Expanding the Self: Buddhism and Psychedelic Therapy $1,200; Psychedelics and Psychoanalysis $1,200. can: Practise ketamine-assisted psychotherapy anywhere in the US, including California, as the psychotherapy half of a collaborative pair. Fluence: 'Ketamine is currently the only legal psychedelic medicine available for clinical therapeutic use in all U.S. states, which makes this training immediately actionable for licensed therapists.'

Provide psychedelic preparation, harm reduction and integration therapy in California with the PHRI certificate — legal in every state, no special credential needed, and already within an LMFT/LCSW/LPCC/psychologist scope. Fluence: 'it is applicable in any state... this training deepens that practice and can be applied immediately within your current professional context.'

Apply for a Colorado state psilocybin facilitator licence, if you complete the whole Psilocybin Facilitation track including the PRATI practicum and the required consultation hours. Fluence International, Inc. is on Colorado DORA's Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs list (didactic: yes; practicum: yes; consultation: available late 2026), verified 2026-08-06. Note that Fluence's track targets the Psilocybin Clinical Facilitator designation, which additionally requires a Colorado psychotherapy, medical or nursing licence.

Earn 42 CE hours per certificate. Fluence 'is approved by the American Psychological Association to sponsor continuing education for psychologists' and 'maintains responsibility for this program and its content.'
Be recognised by KAP care-delivery platforms: Journey Clinical names Fluence as one of the didactic trainings it accepts for therapist onboarding, alongside CIIS, Polaris, MAPS and Alchemy.
cannot: Obtain or replace a psychotherapy licence. Fluence, verbatim: 'This certificate does not grant a psychotherapy license.'

Prescribe or administer ketamine. Fluence, verbatim: 'nor does it confer prescribing authority or the ability to administer ketamine independently.' A prescriber (MD, DO, NP or PA) holds all medical authority.

Administer or supervise the administration of any controlled substance on the PHRI certificate. Fluence, verbatim: 'This certificate does not grant a psychotherapy license, nor does it permit you to administer or supervise the administration of any controlled substance.'

Facilitate psilocybin sessions in California. Psilocybin is Schedule I under California Health & Safety Code §11054 and California has no regulated psilocybin services programme. Fluence: the psilocybin certificate 'does not authorize psilocybin practice in states beyond Colorado (and potentially Oregon pending cross-state equivalency) at this time.'

Use the Fluence psilocybin certificate for Oregon licensure. Fluence does not appear on Oregon Psilocybin Services' list of Current Active Psilocybin Training Programs (15 programs; checked 2026-08-06), and Fluence itself advises: 'if you are primarily interested in practicing in Oregon, the most reliable current path is to pursue an Oregon-specific training or license.' The cross-state equivalency Fluence hopes for is explicitly unguaranteed: 'this outcome depends on legislative and regulatory decisions by both agencies, and we cannot guarantee a timeline or outcome.'

Practise MDMA-assisted therapy. MDMA-assisted therapy is not FDA-approved; Lykos Therapeutics' expanded-access programme is fully enrolled and closed, and Lykos describes itself as still 'focused on pursuing FDA approval'. Consistent with its scope discipline, Fluence's current certificate menu does not include an MDMA facilitation track.
Change anything the California BBS requires or recognises. A Fluence certificate is a school credential; it does not alter your licence, title, or scope.

innertrek.name: Introduction to Psychedelic Facilitation (Level 1) — and the Level 2 Oregon/Colorado licensure track
innertrek.location: Portland / Damascus, Oregon — hybrid, with required in-person practicum in Oregon or Colorado
innertrek.one_line: The only program in this directory whose certificate is attached to a real regulator: InnerTrek's Level 2 track is on the Oregon Health Authority's approved-curriculum list and leads to an actual state psilocybin facilitator licence — but the licence only works inside Oregon, and Oregon's market is contracting.
summary: InnerTrek was founded by Tom Eckert, the architect of Oregon's Measure 109 and chair of the state's first Psilocybin Advisory Board. It sits at Damascus, outside Portland, and it is one of fifteen programs currently on the Oregon Health Authority's list of psilocybin training programs with approved curriculum — verified directly against OHA's own list on 6 August 2026, not against InnerTrek's marketing. It is also on Colorado DORA's list of approved Natural Medicine Training Programs. The Guardian, visiting the campus in January 2024, described it as 'the first government-recognized licensed and operating training program in the world, according to staff.' On the specific question this directory exists to answer — does the certificate do anything a regulator recognises — InnerTrek is the rare yes.

The important structural fact is that InnerTrek runs three levels and only Level 2 is the licensure track. Level 1, the page in the URL above, is a $3,200, roughly eight-week hybrid introduction: 30 hours of online didactic work plus a three-day supervised psilocybin retreat at a licensed Oregon service centre, where students rotate between journeyer and observer roles and legally consume psilocybin. InnerTrek says plainly: 'Completion of Level 1 training does not make students eligible for licensure.' It is a legal, hands-on taste of the work and a $1,000 credit toward Level 2. It is not a step you must take — 'Level 1 Training is not a prerequisite for applying to Level 2.'

Level 2 is the seven-month program that meets Oregon and Colorado requirements: 'over 160 hours of didactic training and 40 hours of supervised practicum,' against Oregon's rule minimum of 128 core hours (OAR 333-333-3050) and 40 practicum hours (OAR 333-333-3070). It runs September 2026 to April 2027 with weekly Wednesday evening Zoom classes, biweekly small home groups of 7-10 students, biweekly skills practice groups, three optional in-person weekend intensives near Portland, and two supervised three-day practicum weekends in Portland or Golden, Colorado, taken in early-to-mid 2027. Residency in Oregon or Colorado is not required and never has been for the Colorado programme; Oregon's own two-year residency requirement for facilitators expired on 1 January 2025 under ORS 475A.325(2)(c). A Californian can do this and can be licensed.

Then comes the part a prospective student should sit with. Oregon's psilocybin programme is contracting. As of June 2026 there were 383 licensed facilitators and only 22 of 35 ever-licensed service centres still operating; the Guardian reported the centre count down by nearly a third by December 2025. Quarterly client numbers hit an all-time low in Q1 2026, down more than 40% year on year, and the average client household income reached $172,000. Amanda Gow, who runs a service centre in Bend and holds both a therapy licence and a facilitator licence, told Lucid News in February 2026 that most of her facilitators see 'one to two psilocybin clients a month' and that 'for facilitators who thought this was going to be their full-time business, it's just not possible.' A facilitator at one Portland centre is paid $560 per session as an independent contractor. Against that, the annual Oregon facilitator licence costs $2,000. And in June 2026 InnerTrek itself let the lease lapse on its own Portland service centre, saying it would focus on training, education and practicum partnerships rather than 'operating a single licensed Service Center location' — a decision that reads differently depending on whether you take it as national expansion or as a training school stepping back from the delivery side of the market it trains people for.

cost.note: $3,200 is Level 1 standard tuition for the Summer 2026 cohort (60 hours of instruction, three-day psilocybin retreat, all materials; psilocybin itself is purchased separately). $400 deposit, refundable to 14 days (elsewhere stated as 5 days) before the start; early-enrolment credits ran $200-$400 off on published deadlines. Level 1 does NOT lead to licensure. The licensure route is Level 2: $6,700 virtual core; +$2,600 for the two required practicums = $9,300 (the Oregon/Colorado licensure pathway); +$600 per optional in-person intensive weekend, or $10,900 for the full virtual + three intensives + practicum bundle. $1,000 deposit, payment plans over 3, 5 or 7 months. Level 1 graduates get $1,000 credited as their Level 2 deposit. On top of tuition, the Oregon licence itself costs a $150 non-refundable application fee plus a $2,000 annual licence fee ($1,000 reduced for veterans, SSI, SNAP or Oregon Health Plan recipients). Total first-year cost of the Oregon licence via InnerTrek is therefore about $11,450 (virtual + practicum) to $13,050 (full experience), before travel and lodging to Oregon or Colorado, which are not priced. InnerTrek also sells a standalone Open Practicum to graduates of other approved schools for $3,000.

innertrek.length: Level 1: described variously on InnerTrek's own pages as four weeks, six weeks and eight weeks — the FAQ's '8 weeks / 60 hours total' is the most specific. Level 2: seven months, September 2026 to April 2027, with practicum weekends running February to early May 2027.
innertrek.hours: Level 1: 60 hours — 30 didactic (8 self-paced online, 4 required live online, plus recorded expert sessions) and 30 hours across a three-day in-person psilocybin retreat. Level 2: 'over 160 hours of didactic training and 40 hours of supervised practicum' (two supervised practicums of 20+ hours each). Oregon's regulatory floor is 128 hours of core training (OAR 333-333-3050) plus 40 practicum hours including at least 30 hours direct practice and 10 hours consultation (OAR 333-333-3070).
innertrek.format: Hybrid. Level 1: self-paced Moodle modules, live Zoom orientation and two home groups, then a three-day in-person psilocybin retreat at a licensed Oregon service centre with prep and integration calls either side. Level 2: weekly live Zoom classes Wednesdays 4-6pm PT, biweekly 90-minute home groups of 7-10 students with a dedicated educator, biweekly optional skills practice groups, weekly optional office hours, three optional in-person weekend intensives at Palais De Leon ten minutes from Portland (recorded for virtual students), and two mandatory in-person supervised practicum weekends in Portland, Oregon or Golden, Colorado. Oregon rules require all practicum, direct practice and consultation to be conducted in person.
innertrek.eligibility: Level 1: at least 21, no formal education required, no prior psychedelic experience required, but applicants 'must demonstrate emotional and psychological readiness during the admissions process.' Anyone worldwide may apply. Participation in the psilocybin journey is required for completion, though someone medically unable to consume may attend the retreat as an observer. Level 2: 'competitive, though there are no formal prerequisites' — InnerTrek says strong applicants tend to be clinicians and healthcare professionals, therapists, counsellors and social workers, alternative healers and wellness practitioners, or people with meaningful experience in space holding. 'Residency in Oregon or Colorado is not required.' Level 1 is not a prerequisite but is 'reviewed favorably.' The underlying Oregon licence requires only: 21 or older, high school diploma or equivalent, criminal background check, completion of an OHA-approved training program, and a passing score on the OPS regulations exam.

curriculum.detail: Introduction to Holding Space (Tom Eckert & Emma Knighton); The Art of Non-Directive Facilitation (Eckert); Ethics & Consent in Altered State Work (Knighton); Preparing a Client for the Journey (Eckert); The Medicine Session: Core Facilitator Skills (Tal Sharabi); Foundations of Group Facilitation (Eckert); Trauma-Informed and Culturally Responsive Care (Knighton); Introduction to Integration and Meaning-Making (Knighton); Facilitator Self-Work and Readiness (Sharabi); The Future of the Movement (Eckert & Nate Howard).

curriculum.module: Level 2 Section 1 — Introduction to Psychedelic Facilitation
curriculum.detail: Historical and current role of plant medicines across wisdom traditions; cultural impact of psychedelics in the West; basic pharmacology and neuroscience of psilocybin; 65 years of research milestones; theories of consciousness and personal transformation; embodied grounded presence; core participant-centred communication skills; problematic facilitator dispositions; self-care systems; working with diverse populations.

curriculum.module: Level 2 Section 2 — Intake, Preparation, and Orientation
curriculum.detail: Rapport and alliance; required intake forms and information-gathering interview; a preparation session covering screening, scope of practice, safety planning and expectation setting; assessing readiness and goodness of fit; orienting a participant to the service sequence; establishing the facilitator's role, responsibilities and authority; dosing strategies; drug and supplement interactions.
Adapting facilitation to diverse populations; effects of psilocybin and other psychedelics on specific mental health populations; current research findings by population.

curriculum.module: Level 2 — Ethics, law and professional standards section
curriculum.detail: Ethical issues of psychedelic facilitation and commitment to core values; working across diverse social locations and cultures; racial justice and systemic inequity in delivery of healthcare and behavioural health services; professional development and leadership presence; 'a detailed understanding of related laws, regulations, and professional standards as they pertain to the rights and ongoing professional obligations of licensed facilitators'; responsible referral and support systems.

Two supervised practicums, 20+ hours each — phase 1 mid-program, phase 2 after the didactic program. Students support participants through psilocybin journeys, experience a facilitated psilocybin journey themselves pending health screening, and practise facilitation skills under supervision within the regulated model. Held in Portland, Oregon or Golden, Colorado. A DORA training licence is required to participate in Colorado practicums. InnerTrek's separately-sold Open Practicum runs Thursday to Sunday with students in triads rotating through journeyer, facilitator and observer roles, capped at 6 students journeying per day and 18 students total.

OAR 333-333-3050 requires at least 128 hours of core instruction with fixed minimums per area: Historical, Traditional and Contemporary Practices 12h; Cultural Equity 12h; Safety, Ethics and Responsibilities 12h; Pharmacology, Neuroscience and Clinical Research 12h; Core Facilitation Skills 16h; Preparation and Orientation 16h; Administration 20h; Integration 12h; Group Facilitation 16h. At least 50% of non-in-person training must be delivered as live online synchronous learning.

can: Complete Level 2 and then apply for a genuine Oregon Health Authority psilocybin facilitator licence. The full requirements are: 21 or older, high school diploma or equivalent, criminal background check, completion of an OHA-approved training program including core training, 40 hours of practicum and a comprehensive skills exam administered by the school, a passing score of 75% or above on the OPS-administered regulations exam (retakeable until passed), a submitted social equity plan, a $150 non-refundable application fee, and a $2,000 annual licence fee ($1,000 if you are a veteran or receive SSI, SNAP or Oregon Health Plan). Renewal is annual and requires four hours of continuing facilitator education. There is no residency requirement — the two-year Oregon residency rule in ORS 475A.325(2)(c) applied only 'until January 1, 2025' and has lapsed.

With that licence, legally sit with clients through preparation, psilocybin administration and integration sessions — but only at an Oregon-licensed psilocybin service centre, with the client physically in Oregon.

Also qualify for Colorado natural medicine facilitator licensure. InnerTrek is on Colorado DORA's approved training list, and InnerTrek states graduates are eligible for licensure in both states. Colorado's requirements are set by DORA and are not identical to Oregon's — verify separately.

Do Level 1 alone as a legal, supervised, first-hand psilocybin experience with instruction wrapped around it, useful for a California therapist who wants to know what the state actually feels like before recommending or integrating it.

Bring the training back to California as integration work and as ketamine-assisted psychotherapy competence — which is what most Californian graduates will actually monetise, since neither requires an Oregon licence.
cannot: Change your California licence or scope of practice. An Oregon psilocybin facilitator licence is a separate, parallel credential from a separate state's health authority. The California BBS neither recognises it nor is affected by it.

Do anything with psilocybin in California. Psilocybin and psilocyn are Schedule I under California Health & Safety Code §11054(d)(18)-(19) and Schedule I federally. An Oregon licence is territorially useless outside Oregon: you cannot transport product, treat a Californian client remotely, or hold sessions in California.

Practise as a therapist during the psilocybin work, even in Oregon. OHA is explicit: licensed facilitators 'may not practice on other professional licenses while providing preparation, administration, or integration sessions.' Oregon's HB 2387 relaxed this from 1 January 2026 — but only for people licensed by seven named Oregon boards (Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists, Naturopathic Medicine, Psychology, Medical Board, Nursing, Licensed Social Workers, Pharmacy). A California LMFT is not covered by any of them. Psychedelic Alpha notes that OPS does not recognise out-of-state licensure for regulatory purposes.
Get licensed on Level 1 alone. 'Completion of Level 1 training does not make students eligible for licensure.'
Rely on the Level 2 didactic-only option ($6,700) for licensure. The 40-hour supervised practicum is a regulatory requirement (OAR 333-333-3070) and it costs an extra $2,600.

Direct the client's experience. Oregon's model is statutorily non-directive: facilitators 'support clients through psilocybin services without directing the client experience.' This is a real constraint on a therapist trained to intervene.
Count on making a living at it. See voices below — this is the single most important thing to understand before spending $11,000-$13,000.
scope.disclaimer_quote: Completion of Level 1 training does not make students eligible for licensure. While Level 1 is not a prerequisite for Level 2, it is reviewed favorably during the application process.

faculty: Tom Eckert, MS — founder and executive director; a psychotherapist who was the architect of Measure 109, led the 2020 campaign, and chaired Oregon's Governor-appointed Psilocybin Advisory Board in its first year. He also established the Sheri Eckert Foundation. He is the reason this school exists and the reason it was first through OHA's door.

Emma Knighton, MA — somatic trauma therapist and psychedelic-assisted therapist; co-founder of the American Psychedelic Practitioners Association; teaches nationally on consent and trauma-informed care in psychedelic services. She carries the ethics and consent material, which given the field's history is the most consequential part of the curriculum.

Tal Sharabi, MA — psychotherapist trained in psychedelic psychotherapy and research at CIIS, ketamine-assisted psychotherapy through Polaris Insight Center, and MAPS-certified MDMA-assisted therapy Parts A-D. The most directly relevant faculty member for a California therapist, because her own training path is the one a Californian would recognise.
Jason Foster, MA — Seattle private-practice therapist, former lead supervisor with the Zendo Project, 15+ years in psychedelic facilitation and education; trained in Core Energetics.
Elyse Gardner, MA — licensed transpersonal psychotherapist and retreat leader; Director of Operations for the nonprofit Right To Heal.
David Kahl — entrepreneur, executive coach and licensed psilocybin facilitator who designs and leads multi-day psilocybin retreats; brings group facilitation and retreat design.
Lisa Snyder — InnerTrek graduate, state-licensed facilitator in both Oregon and Colorado, and InnerTrek's Director of Operations; a live example of the credential's ceiling.
Nate Howard — director of operations, described by the Guardian as having played a large role in developing Oregon's programme.
Leonie Wolff, RN and Henry Fields — experiential facilitators for Level 1 retreats; both InnerTrek graduates and licensed facilitators.

voices.text: The attrition is setting in, and a lot of people are not renewing their license because it is hard to make money.
voices.who: Gary Bracelin, owner of Drop Thesis Psilocybin Service Center, quoted in The Guardian, December 2025

voices.text: For facilitators who thought this was going to be their full-time business, it's just not possible. … Most of Bendable's facilitators see one to two psilocybin clients a month. It's not their full-time business. … I just spent $2,000 yesterday for my license for the year, whereas my therapy license is $300 every two years.
voices.who: Amanda Gow, co-founder of Bendable Therapy service center, Bend OR, and a dual-licensed therapist and facilitator, quoted in Lucid News, February 2026

voices.text: After a wave of people trained to become facilitators, many dropped off because there weren't enough clients. … It's like a cart before the horse.
voices.who: Max Kelemen, executive director of the Portland Psychedelic Society, quoted in The Guardian, December 2025

voices.text: There are still growing concerns that the number of trained facilitators is becoming unsustainable and increasingly misaligned with the number of licensed service centers and, by extension, available facilitator roles. Many are already struggling to secure full-time employment within OPS. … Training programs typically range from $4,500 to $12,000 (with the mean sitting around $10,000), with practicum components adding another couple of thousand dollars. … Altogether, the first year can easily exceed $10,000.
voices.who: Psychedelic Alpha, Oregon Psilocybin Services Tracker, updated through Q1/June 2026

voices.text: His facilitators are independent contractors paid $560 per session.
voices.who: The Guardian on Dr Eric Lee's Space Psychedelic Center, Portland, December 2025 — the only published per-session facilitator pay figure found

voices.text: We've been focused solely on one license type (service centers), and we're failing to talk about the story of almost 400 licensed facilitators and the fact that this model established a new healthcare profession. … From a safety standpoint, and a service center's ability to deliver and provide services, things seem to be going quite well.
voices.who: Angela Allbee, Oregon Psilocybin Services Section Manager, Oregon Health Authority, quoted in Lucid News, February 2026

voices.text: I push back on the idea that these closures are signaling any type of issue with the program being in jeopardy. What we are seeing is exactly what early-stage market maturation in the first couple of years looks like for any licensed and regulated industry.
voices.who: Sam Chapman, Executive Director, Center for Psychedelic Policy, quoted in Lucid News, February 2026

voices.text: But first, they'll need to complete a program like the one taking place at InnerTrek – the first government-recognized licensed and operating training program in the world, according to staff.

voices.text: June 2026 marks the successful completion of the InnerTrek Center for Psilocybin Services' three-year lease. As InnerTrek continues to grow as a national training organization, we have made the decision to focus our energy on training, education, and practicum partnerships across the United States rather than renewing and operating a single licensed Service Center location. … the space has supported more than 1,270 clients and participants.
voices.who: InnerTrek's own service centre page, 2026. Psychedelic Alpha independently records a service-centre licence expiring or surrendered in June 2026 'with the latter shifting focus to facilitator training and education.' Note that InnerTrek's Level 2 page still advertises practicums at 'InnerTrek's licensed psilocybin service center in Portland, Oregon.'

voices.text: One editorial in the Journal of the American Academy of Psychiatry noted that Oregon's psilocybin training requires just 25% of the 625 hours mandated for a massage therapist license. … while the OHA approves training programs, it does not regulate individual facilitator licensure. The burden of evaluating and endorsing candidates falls on the training programs themselves, many of which are small, privately-run enterprises. … just one facilitator license application has been denied to date.
voices.who: Psychedelic Alpha, Oregon Psilocybin Services Tracker, 2026 — a structural criticism that applies to every OHA-approved school including InnerTrek

innertrek.status_2026: Enrolling — verified 6 August 2026. gaps: Level 2 cohort size. InnerTrek publishes home-group size (7-10 students with 1 educator) and practicum caps (6 journeying per day, 18 students total), but not total cohort enrolment.
Whether Level 2 practicum tuition includes the psilocybin product. Level 1 states psilocybin 'is provided at the retreat and purchased separately'; the Level 2 tuition breakdown does not address it.

Where InnerTrek's Oregon practicums now take place, since its own service centre closed in June 2026 and the Level 2 page still names it. The Open Practicum page says only 'Portland, OR' or 'Golden, Colorado.'
Lodging and travel costs. On-site lodging for intensives is listed as 'TBA'; nothing is published for practicum weekends. For a Californian this is a material and unpriced part of the total.

Graduate outcomes. Neither InnerTrek nor OHA publishes how many InnerTrek graduates obtain licences, how many are actively working, or what they earn. The $560/session figure is from one centre reported by the Guardian.

Colorado's specific licensure requirements, fees and hour counts. I verified only that InnerTrek is on DORA's approved list and that a DORA training licence is required before a Colorado practicum; DORA's fee schedule and full requirements were not established here.

Any statement from the California Board of Behavioral Sciences about California licensees holding an Oregon psilocybin facilitator licence, or working psilocybin sessions in Oregon. Nothing on bbs.ca.gov mentions psychedelics, psilocybin or ketamine. Oregon's HB 2387 disciplinary protections explicitly cover only seven Oregon boards, so a California LMFT's exposure to their own board is genuinely unresolved and worth a lawyer, not a directory entry.

Independent student reviews of InnerTrek. Reddit is unreachable from this environment and general web-search engines were blocked; the criticism recorded above is programme-level and market-level, not school-level.

integrative-psychiatry-institute.name: IPI Psychedelic Therapy Level I Certification (Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy Training)
integrative-psychiatry-institute.location: Niwot, Colorado — training delivered fully online; the only in-person component is a separately-priced 4-day psilocybin practicum in Eugene, Oregon
integrative-psychiatry-institute.one_line: A four-month, fully online, 140-hour certificate that explicitly states it is not approved for Oregon or Colorado licensure — but IPI's separate $3,000 psilocybin practicum in Eugene turns it into a combined programme that does appear on Oregon's approved-curriculum list.
summary: IPI runs what is probably the highest-volume psychedelic therapy training aimed at working clinicians in the US: it claims 2,200+ providers trained. The current offering is 'Level I Certification', a four-month online course running 4 September to 11 December 2026. Nothing about it requires travel. You get a set of asynchronous 'Foundations' modules before the start date, two one-day live virtual intensives that bookend the course, a weekly 60-minute Tuesday lecture, a bi-weekly two-hour Thursday seminar in breakout rooms, a weekly hour-long small group, and a private forum. Everything is recorded and stays available for a year after the programme ends. IPI counts the whole package as 140 hours, 55 of them live.

The tuition is $7,000, discounted to $5,000 for registrations before 31 August 2026, with payment plans discussed on an admissions call. That buys the online course and two advertised bonuses: 40 hours of recorded real ketamine and psilocybin sessions, and a 20-hour 'Psychedelic Therapy B-School' on running a practice. Continuing education is real and externally accredited: up to 49.0 credits through AKH Inc., which is jointly accredited by ACCME, ACPE and ANCC, with psychologist credit through APA and social-work credit through ASWB ACE. For a California LMFT that matters — the BBS recognises APA and ASWB as CE approval agencies, and requires 36 CE hours per two-year renewal.

The experiential component is a separate purchase, not part of the certificate price. IPI operates its own Oregon psilocybin service centre, Conscious Encounters, in downtown Eugene, and sells a 'Certificate in Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy': a 4-day, 40-hour practicum, Tuesday to Friday, capped at 24 people, for $3,000 (payment plan $500/month), plus $46–$90 paid on-site for the psilocybin itself because Oregon rules require the service centre to sell it separately. You get one personal dosing session (up to 35mg psilocybin analyte) and act as student facilitator in a second, with Oregon-licensed facilitators as the primary facilitators. This is the only in-person, hands-on part of IPI's offering.

The scope claim on the sales page is unusually careful for this field — IPI says in plain text that Level I is not approved by Colorado DORA or the Oregon Health Authority. That is true of Level I on its own. But OHA's live list of training programmes with approved curriculum does contain an IPI entry, listed as 'IPI Psychedelic Assisted Therapy Training with an Advanced Certificate in Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy', registered to Niwot, CO, pointing at this same page. So the combined online course plus psilocybin practicum is an OHA-approved curriculum; the online course by itself is not. IPI's public marketing does not spell this distinction out, and a prospective student should get it in writing from both IPI and OHA before paying.

cost.note: Regular tuition $7,000; 'Registration Discount until August 31, 2026' of $5,000. 'Additional discounts and payment plans may be available on your admissions call.' The 4-day psilocybin practicum in Eugene, Oregon is a separate $3,000 (or $500/month over 6 months), and does not include the psilocybin itself, which the service centre must sell on-site separately for an estimated $46–$90.

integrative-psychiatry-institute.length: 4 months. The 2026 cohort runs 4 September 2026 (Virtual Intensive I) to 11 December 2026 (Virtual Intensive II). The optional psilocybin practicum is 4 days, scheduled separately. Note the URL still says 'year-long' — a legacy slug; the programme described on the page is four months.
integrative-psychiatry-institute.hours: 140 hours of learning, of which 55 hours are live virtual sessions. Advertised on top of that: 40 hours of recorded real psychedelic therapy sessions and a 20-hour business module. The Eugene psilocybin practicum is 40 hours over four days, 8:00am–6:00pm.
integrative-psychiatry-institute.format: Fully online. Asynchronous 'Foundations of Psychedelic Therapy' modules available before the start date; one-day Live Virtual Intensive I (4 Sept 2026) and II (11 Dec 2026); weekly 60-minute online lectures (Tuesdays 9:00am MT); bi-weekly 120-minute large group seminars in breakout rooms (Thursdays 9:00–11:00am MT); weekly 60-minute small 'home group' Zooms; a private community forum. All sessions recorded, library access for one year after the programme ends. The only in-person element is the separately-priced Eugene, Oregon psilocybin practicum.
integrative-psychiatry-institute.eligibility: Open to LMFTs. IPI states it is 'now accepting applications from' Professional Clinical Counselors (LPC), Clinical Psychologists (PhD/PsyD), Physicians (MD/DO), Nurse Practitioners (NP), Marriage and Family Therapists (LMFT), Clinical Social Workers (LCSW), Physician Assistants (PA), and Pre-licensed Therapists (MA). It is not restricted to prescribers — the majority of the named alumni and testimonials on the page are LMFTs, LCSWs and LPCs. Pre-licensed associates are explicitly eligible. Admission runs through a 'See If I Qualify' form and an admissions call.

curriculum.detail: Ethics in psychedelic-assisted therapy; integrating ketamine-assisted therapy into a clinical practice; protecting boundaries in psychedelic sessions; professional liability.
Therapist self-regulation; how to work with the 'Inner Healing Intelligence'; how to be with non-ordinary states of consciousness; navigating the safe uses of therapeutic touch.
Indigenous history of psychedelic use; diversity, equity and inclusion in psychedelic medicine; confronting bias and cultural appropriation; the intersection of capitalism and psychedelics.

History and current status of MDMA, psilocybin, ketamine and other psychedelic research; screening and monitoring for patient psychological safety; patient education on benefits and challenges; chemistry and pharmacology of psychedelics.
Mindfulness and intention-setting practices; physical preparation; set and setting; establishing safety measures.
Addressing an expanded spectrum of root causes; mind-body practices to support integration; somatic therapy techniques and parts work; values-based behaviour change.

curriculum.module: Certificate in Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy (separate 4-day practicum, Eugene, Oregon)
curriculum.detail: 40 hours over four days at IPI's own Oregon psilocybin service centre, Conscious Encounters, capped at 24 people. Preparation (large-group and peer-to-peer), two dosing days with a personal dosing session in group format (up to 35mg psilocybin analyte, roughly 3–4 grams of raw material, with an 11am booster) and a turn as student facilitator in the second session, group and peer integration, plus emergency protocol training, yoga and movement. Oregon-licensed facilitators act as the primary facilitators. A 60-minute online group integration follows. $3,000, psilocybin purchased separately on-site.

can: Keep practising as a California LMFT, with a school-issued certificate that says you completed a 140-hour course. It is a credential from IPI, not from a regulator.

Count up to 49.0 continuing education credits toward your BBS renewal. IPI's CE is provided through AKH Inc. (jointly accredited by ACCME, ACPE and ANCC), with psychologist credit via APA and social-work credit via ASWB ACE — and the California BBS recognises APA and ASWB as CE approval agencies for its 36-hour-per-renewal requirement. That is the one concrete, regulator-recognised thing this certificate does in California.

Practise ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in California, working alongside a physician, NP or PA who prescribes and is responsible for the ketamine. You do not prescribe. Nothing about the certificate creates this ability — an LMFT can already do KAP in collaboration with a prescriber — but the training is aimed squarely at it, and IPI is candid that ketamine is the only modality available now.
Offer psychedelic preparation and integration therapy, which is ordinary psychotherapy about a client's experience and needs no special credential.

Have a personal, legal psilocybin experience and a supervised turn as facilitator, if you also buy the $3,000 Eugene practicum. Under Oregon's framework this is psilocybin services at a licensed service centre, not therapy.

Pursue an Oregon psilocybin facilitator licence off the back of it — but only via the combined pathway. OHA's live list of training programmes with approved curriculum includes 'IPI Psychedelic Assisted Therapy Training with an Advanced Certificate in Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy'. Approved curriculum is one of six requirements; you also need to be 21+, hold a high school diploma, pass a criminal background check, complete the programme's practicum and comprehensive exam, and pass an OHA-administered exam.
Be more credible to a ketamine clinic that hires. IPI is the highest-volume trainer in this space and clinic job listings recognise the name; that is a market fact, not a regulatory one.
cannot: Change your BBS licence, scope of practice or title in any way. The BBS does not issue, recognise or require a psychedelic-therapy credential, and does not maintain a list of them.

Administer, prescribe, supply or possess psilocybin or MDMA in California. Both remain Schedule I federally and there is no California therapeutic framework — SB 58 was vetoed in October 2023 and the state's 2025 action was a bill to accelerate study of psychedelics for PTSD, not to legalise therapeutic use.
Use the Level I certificate on its own for Oregon or Colorado licensure. IPI says so itself, verbatim, on the sales page: Level I 'is not an approved training' by DORA or OHA.
Get anywhere with Colorado. IPI does not appear on DORA's list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs (checked 6 August 2026).

Practise as a psychotherapist while facilitating in Oregon, if you go that route. OHA is explicit: licensed facilitators 'may not practice on other professional licenses while providing preparation, administration, or integration sessions to clients.' An Oregon facilitator licence is a separate, non-clinical role — it is not LMFT work with mushrooms.

Do anything with MDMA outside a research protocol or MAPS' expanded access. The FDA issued a complete response letter on Lykos' MDMA-assisted therapy application in August 2024 and there has been no approval since. IPI's own page says MDMA and psilocybin 'may only be a year away from a full FDA approval' — that is IPI's marketing claim, not a regulatory position, and similar claims have been made for several years.
scope.disclaimer_quote: While ketamine is the only nationwide psychedelic treatment available, MDMA and Psilocybin may only be a year away from a full FDA approval. However, Level I certification is not an approved training by the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies (DORA) for purposes of licensure under the Colorado Natural Medicine and Natural Medicine Product Act, nor is it an approved training by the Oregon Health Authority (OHA) for licensure under the Oregon Psilocybin Services Act.

mind-foundation-apt.name: Augmented Psychotherapy Training (APT)
mind-foundation-apt.org: MIND Foundation gGmbH (partner of OVID Clinic Berlin)
mind-foundation-apt.location: Berlin, Germany — hybrid (three on-site intensive weeks in Berlin + weekly online sessions)
mind-foundation-apt.one_line: A 15-month, €15,000 European training in psychedelic-augmented psychotherapy, with three residential weeks in Berlin — rigorous and explicitly anti-underground, but it confers nothing legally in the United States, and its supervised personal-experience component is ketamine and breathwork, not psilocybin.
summary: The MIND Foundation is a Berlin non-profit tied to the OVID Clinic and to German psilocybin research (the EPIsoDE and DiMension trials). Its Augmented Psychotherapy Training is a 15-month program built around two named things: 'Psychedelic-Augmented Psychotherapy' (inducing altered states inside a therapy process) and 'Integration-Focused Psychotherapy' (working with psychedelic experiences that happened outside the therapy room). The structure is three on-site intensive weeks in Berlin — for the ninth, English-language cohort: 7–13 Nov 2026, 3–9 Jul 2027, 19–25 Feb 2028 — plus weekly online sessions on Thursdays at 19:30 CET for the whole 15 months, plus a self-paced online course (Molecules) and a required four-day integration workshop (Beyond Experience). Cohorts cap at 32 people. Certification requires at least 80% attendance.

Tuition is EUR 15,000 paid in one lump sum, or EUR 16,800 across six installments — the site owner's recollection of 'roughly €15,000' is correct and verified on MIND's own admissions page. That figure explicitly excludes accommodation, travel, and the compulsory Beyond Experience workshop, which is listed at €690. So for a Californian the real outlay is €15,000 tuition + €690 workshop + three round-trips to Berlin + roughly three weeks of lodging and three weeks out of practice, spread over 15 months. MIND is a registered German non-profit and states that APT revenue cannot be extracted by individuals.

On the question that matters most for this record: the APT does include a supervised personal experience of an altered state, and it happens in Berlin during the intensive weeks — but it is ketamine and non-pharmacological methods (breathwork, guided imagery, music, stroboscopic light), not psilocybin. MIND's own FAQ is unambiguous: 'The self-experience curriculum in APT currently includes ketamine as well as all of the non-pharmacological methods mentioned above.' Germany has no legal framework for supervised psilocybin outside of clinical trials, and MIND says so directly. The program teaches about psilocybin and LSD; it does not give you psilocybin. Anyone choosing APT specifically to get a legal psilocybin session should not; that is not what this is.

What APT actually is, judged on its own terms, is a serious clinical training with unusually explicit gatekeeping. Applicants must be 25 or older, hold one of nine listed professional qualifications, and produce a police clearance certificate showing no drug or capital convictions. MIND's published exclusion criteria include 'uncritical attitude towards ideas that can be evaluated as pseudoscience, charlatanry, conspiracy theories, or esotericism' and 'illegal underground therapy practice.' For a California LMFT, the honest calculus is: you will get a deep, research-adjacent, European clinical education and a network of European clinicians; you will not get anything a US regulator, a US insurer, or a US employer is obliged to recognise; and the one modality you can practise in California when you get home — ketamine-assisted psychotherapy — can be trained for domestically at a fraction of the cost and none of the airfare.
modality: General/substance-agnostic (breathwork, guided imagery, music, stroboscopic light)

cost.note: 'Standard price: EUR 15,000.- for the complete training.' Single payment EUR 15,000; payment in six installments EUR 16,800 total. Tuition explicitly does NOT cover accommodation, travel expenses, or the compulsory self-experience workshop Beyond Experience (listed at €690 regular price on its own page). GDP-adjusted discount of 5–20% available on request for applicants working in countries with significantly lower GDP than Germany; a limited number of scholarships per cohort. The self-paced Molecules course (€495 standalone, listed with 35 CME points) is included in APT tuition — if you already paid for it, that amount is discounted from tuition. Verified 2026-08-06.

mind-foundation-apt.hours: MIND does not publish a total contact-hour figure. Published components: three on-site intensive weeks in Berlin (7 days each per the listed cohort dates); weekly online sessions on Thursdays at 19:30 CET/CEST across the full 15 months; the self-paced Molecules course; the four-day Beyond Experience workshop. Minimum 80% attendance required for certification. CME: the FAQ states CME credits have been granted for Molecules (37) and Beyond Experience (39); the Molecules page itself lists '35 CME-Points'.
mind-foundation-apt.format: Hybrid. Three residential intensive weeks in Berlin (theory units, practical exercises, role-play, and self-experience in altered states — MIND states these cannot be attended remotely) plus weekly online lectures, a journal club, small-group online mentoring (4–6 participants, led by experienced therapists, including elements of clinical supervision), and meditation training. Maximum 32 participants per cohort. Offered in English and German.
mind-foundation-apt.eligibility: Applicants must hold one of nine listed qualifications. Two tiers, and MIND is explicit about the difference. Qualified after certification to 'work independently and lead multiprofessional teams': medical doctor with training in psychotherapy (e.g. specialist in psychiatry); licensed psychotherapist. Qualified only to 'work in multiprofessional teams under the supervision' of one of the above: medical doctor without completed psychotherapy training; clinical psychologist without completed psychotherapy training; family or couple therapist with a relevant BA/BSc minimum; psychological counsellor/coach with a relevant BA/BSc minimum; complementary therapist (music, dance, art therapy) with a relevant BA/BSc minimum; licensed psychiatric nurse; social worker/addiction therapist. 'Applicants without any of the above professional qualifications are not eligible for admission.' Further requirements for certification: minimum age 25, and a police clearance certificate (not previously convicted for capital crimes or drug offenses). Application is a cover letter (max 2 pages) plus a short CV, then an online interview. Published exclusion criteria: uncritical attitude toward pseudoscience/charlatanry/conspiracy theories/esotericism; illegal underground therapy practice; general rejection of conventional medicine or psychotherapy; political or religious extremism.

curriculum.module: Learning format: three on-site intensive weeks (Berlin)
curriculum.detail: 'The on-site curriculum includes a varied program of theory units, practical exercises, and self-experience in altered states of consciousness.' Cannot be attended remotely because of the experiential content (role-play, exercises, self-experience with ketamine and breathwork).

Lectures with leading international experts; a journal club on psychedelic therapy and research; small-group mentoring sessions (4–6 participants) with psychedelic-experienced therapists that focus on case discussion and include elements of clinical supervision; and meditation training. Thursdays, 19:30 CET/CEST.

curriculum.module: Molecules (self-paced online course, included in tuition)
curriculum.detail: MIND's graduate-level certificate course on 'the neurobiology and pharmacology of psychoactive drugs, applied knowledge about psychedelic therapy and drug-related emergencies, and an extensive overview over psychedelic research.' Listed at €495 standalone with 35 CME-Points.

curriculum.module: Beyond Experience (compulsory 4-day integration workshop, NOT included in tuition)
curriculum.detail: 'A 4-day-intensive workshop... The focus is on the integration of experiences acquired in expanded states of consciousness, both substance and non-substance induced.' Listed at €690 regular price; reduced 'Access tickets' of 25–100% off available by application. Held in Berlin, Amsterdam, Mallorca, and expanding to Romania and Portugal.

1. Apply psychotherapeutic concepts, methods, and attitudes in psychedelic therapy. 2. Understand the scientific, medical, and philosophical foundations of psychedelic therapy. 3. Understand the diverse cultural, social, and medical history of psychedelics. 4. Comply with legal requirements and address ethical challenges. 5. Understand and incorporate existential aspects of psychedelic experiences. 6. Cultivate a learning-oriented attitude toward psychedelic self-experience and reflect on its relevance for shaping therapeutic processes.

7. Cooperate and communicate professionally with colleagues in multi-professional teams and health care institutions. 8. Prevent and mitigate adverse effects of psychedelics. 9. Screen patients and plan treatments. 10. Prepare patients for psychedelic experiences. 11. Induce and accompany psychedelic experiences in appropriate settings. 12. Support patients in the integration of psychedelic experiences and assist their transition to the post-treatment phase.

MIND's FAQ, verbatim: 'We teach a broad scope of methods to induce altered states of consciousness: Pharmacological methods include classical psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD, etc.) and atypical psychedelics (ketamine). Non-pharmacological methods include breathwork, guided imagery, music, and stroboscopic light. The self-experience curriculum in APT currently includes ketamine as well as all of the non-pharmacological methods mentioned above.' So: the training teaches about psilocybin and LSD but the supervised personal experience is ketamine plus non-drug methods, delivered on-site in Berlin.

'The APT program takes a transtheoretical approach... No specific psychotherapeutic orientation or school is emphasized over others.' Organised around Klaus Grawe's general change mechanisms: resource activation, therapeutic relationship, problem actuation, motivational clarification/clarification of meaning, mastery.

can: Practise integration-focused psychotherapy in California — working with clients before and after psychedelic experiences that happen outside your office. This needs no certificate at all; it is already inside an LMFT/LCSW/LPCC/psychologist scope. APT gives you a structured framework for it, not permission.

Use the non-pharmacological methods the program teaches (breathwork, guided imagery, music, stroboscopic light) with clients, subject to your own competence and your board's scope rules. MIND: 'While non-pharmacological methods are at your disposal wherever you practice...'

Work as the psychotherapy half of a ketamine-assisted psychotherapy team in California, where a physician, NP, or PA does the prescribing and medical monitoring — but note APT is not a KAP-specific training and there are US programs built exactly for this.

Be a credible candidate for research-adjacent roles, European clinics, and clinical-trial site work, and hold a training credential from an organisation with real ties to German psilocybin trials (EPIsoDE, DiMension).

Say honestly that you have had a supervised, legal, medically screened personal experience of an altered state as part of a professional training — a ketamine session, in Berlin, under German medical supervision.
cannot: Administer or possess psilocybin, LSD, or MDMA anywhere in the United States. Psilocybin and LSD are Schedule I under California Health & Safety Code §11054; there is no California therapeutic exemption.

Prescribe or administer ketamine in California. You are a therapist, not a prescriber, and MIND's own certificate 'does not legally entitle you to work with medications or other pharmacological substances.'

Use APT toward Oregon psilocybin facilitator licensure. MIND Foundation does not appear on Oregon Psilocybin Services' list of Current Active Psilocybin Training Programs (15 programs listed; checked 2026-08-06).
Use APT toward Colorado natural-medicine facilitator licensure. MIND Foundation does not appear on Colorado DORA's list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs (checked 2026-08-06).
Change anything about your California BBS licence, scope of practice, or renewal requirements. The BBS neither recognises nor requires this certificate.

Count the training toward California CE hours as a matter of course. MIND's credits are German CME points for Molecules and Beyond Experience; they are not stated to be APA-sponsor CE, which is the route the BBS accepts.
scope.disclaimer_quote: After successfully completing the APT Program, participants are awarded a certificate in Psychedelic Therapy (Integration-Focused and Psychedelic-Augmented Psychotherapy). Depending on their professional background, certified professionals are qualified to work independently and lead multiprofessional teams providing psychedelic therapy, or to work in such multiprofessional teams under the supervision of a medical doctor with training in psychotherapy or a licensed psychotherapist. The certificate covers breathwork-, ketamine-, and psychedelic-augmented psychotherapy. However, the certificate does not legally entitle you to work with medications or other pharmacological substances. This authorization is acquired through country- and region-specific approbations and is subject to corresponding legal regulations. We strictly require all APT participants to comply with the legal regulations applicable at their respective place of work.
