summary: Read the organisational chart before the curriculum. Naropa University does not offer this programme any more. In December 2024 Naropa announced the separation and renaming of the Naropa Center for Psychedelic Studies into an independent 501(c)(3), the Memoru Center for Visionary Healing Arts, a collaboration between the NCPS founding team and Boulder MDMA researchers Marcela Ot'alora G., Bruce Poulter and Sara Gael Beauregard. All NCPS staff and operations moved. Naropa's own transition FAQ gives the reason plainly: 'Because Naropa receives federal funding and is subject to federal regulations, we cannot administer these substances or operate related clinics.' What remains at Naropa is a BA Psychedelic Studies minor, some existing graduate courses, and an exploratory natural-medicines track in the Master of Divinity. The Naropa PFT page is still live and still advertises a cohort that started 21 January 2025 with applications that closed 24 November 2024 — a stale page, not a current offering. If you are pricing this programme in 2026 you are pricing Memoru.

The regulatory position is the reason this record matters, and it is genuinely different from almost every other training in this set. Colorado has a real, operating, licensed facilitator profession under Proposition 122 and SB23-290, administered by DORA's Division of Professions and Occupations. As of 6 August 2026 the DORA list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs includes 'Memoru Center for Visionary Healing Arts, Boulder, CO' with didactic, practicum training and consultation all marked Yes — one of only about fifteen approved programmes statewide. 'Naropa University' does not appear on that list. So the training pathway is intact, it just has a different name on the certificate.

Oregon, however, has fallen away. Naropa's page still claims Oregon approval, and the December 2024 press release said Memoru 'has inherited Naropa's Colorado state certification to offer psilocybin training and transferring the Oregon certification is in process'. It did not complete. Oregon Psilocybin Services' live list of training programmes with approved curriculum, checked 6 August 2026, contains fifteen programmes and neither Naropa nor Memoru is among them (UC Berkeley's BCSP and CIIS both still are). Memoru's own training page now says only that its programme 'is designed to prepare facilitators for licensure in Colorado and we remain open to complying with additional state models in the future'. Treat every Oregon claim on the Naropa page as expired.

What Colorado licensure actually costs you in hours: 150 hours of approved didactic training with a topic-by-topic minimum set by rule (25 hours ethics and Colorado natural medicine rules, 25 hours physical and mental health and state, 10 each on relational boundaries and touch, trauma-informed care, Indigenous/social/cultural considerations, preparation, administration, integration, group facilitation and facilitator self-care, 5 each on best practices, drug effects and interactions, suicide risk and screening), plus 40 hours of supervised practice (the practicum), plus 40 hours of consultation with a licensed Consultant, of which 10 must be on ethical issues, completed within two years of the Training Licence being issued. You also need to be 21+, hold current Basic Life Support certification, clear criminal-history screening, complete the Healthcare Professions Profile, and pay a non-refundable application fee. Notably, DORA does not publish a state examination requirement for facilitators — that is an Oregon feature, not a Colorado one. Naropa's page states a 50-hour consultation figure; DORA's own March 2025 facilitator guide says 40, so use 40. Licences run to 31 January annually and continuing education is required — DORA held a stakeholder meeting on 20 August 2026 on revising the CE rule, so treat the exact annual CE hours as in flux.

For a California LMFT, LCSW or LPCC the answer to 'what can I do with this' is: work in Colorado, on Colorado's terms, under a Colorado licence, and nothing at all in California. Colorado's Facilitator tier has no clinical-licence requirement, so a Californian can complete the training and license as a plain Facilitator — but a Facilitator explicitly 'cannot engage in psychotherapy, the practice of medicine, or any secondary profession that would require the use of touch beyond the scope allowed by 4 CCR 755-1 6.6, Supportive Touch'. The higher Clinical Facilitator tier, which does let you practise your secondary profession alongside natural medicine services, requires an active Colorado licence as a PSY, LSW, LCSW, LMFT, LPC, LAC, MD, DO, APN, NP or PA. A California LMFT licence does not satisfy that; you would need Colorado licensure. Colorado also offers licensure by endorsement to someone holding an Oregon facilitator licence in good standing for a year plus a valid Colorado secondary licence.

cost.note: No tuition figure is published anywhere. Naropa's PFT programme page, its application-and-policies page (which now redirects to the psychedelic-studies transition FAQ), Memoru's training page at memorucenter.org and Memoru's site at memoru.com all describe the programme without stating a price. The practicum and consultation are separately priced add-ons and were listed as 'Dates and Costs TBD' even when Naropa ran the programme. Colorado's DORA application fee is described as required and non-refundable but the amount is not published on DORA's public web pages. The one price Memoru does publish is unrelated: its consultation/supervision group with Sara Lewis, PhD, LCSW is $60 per group for pre-licensed therapists and $80 for licensed therapists.

naropa-psilocybin-facilitator.length: Six months of didactic training, plus a separately scheduled 40-hour practicum and then 40 hours of consultation spread over the two years following the Training Licence.
naropa-psilocybin-facilitator.hours: 150 hours of didactic instruction (Colorado's rule minimum) + 40 hours supervised practicum + 40 hours consultation, of which 10 hours must address ethical issues arising in the trainee's work. Weekly workload during the didactic phase: a two-hour live class, a two-hour Pod group twice monthly, and four to five hours of independent work.
naropa-psilocybin-facilitator.format: Hybrid. As run by Naropa: virtual, with required live attendance — weekly live classes on Zoom, Wednesdays 5:00-7:00pm Mountain Time, plus small-group 'Pods' on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month with three time-slot options (12:00-2:00, 4:00-6:00 or 6:00-8:00pm MT) assigned with time zones in mind, plus asynchronous content, reflection journalling and assignments. Attendance at live classes and Pods was mandatory. Memoru now describes the format as 'online learning + in-person retreats' with supervised practicum, consultation and ongoing mentorship.
naropa-psilocybin-facilitator.eligibility: Set to match the state rules rather than to gatekeep clinically: at least 21 years of age, a high school diploma or equivalent, US resident, and a professional licence in good standing only if applicable — that is, only for those pursuing Colorado's Clinical Facilitator tier. No clinical degree, no prior therapy experience and no psychedelic experience are required for the plain Facilitator tier. Colorado's Clinical Facilitator tier additionally requires an active Colorado licence as a Psychologist, LSW, LCSW, LMFT, LPC, LAC, MD, DO, APN/NP or PA — a California licence does not qualify.

curriculum.module: Module 1 — Traditional Roots, Healing Justice, Health Equity
curriculum.detail: Traditional cultural use and decolonial approaches to psilocybin facilitation; racial justice and intergenerational trauma; empathy versus compassion and facilitator self-care.

curriculum.module: Module 2 — Presence, Ethics, Harm Reduction, Boundaries
curriculum.detail: Facilitator best practices and core competencies; mitigating risk; abuse of power and ethical facilitation.

curriculum.module: Module 3 — Trauma-Informed Care, Establishing Rapport, Screening and Intake
curriculum.detail: Trauma physiology; trauma-informed communication skills; determining client eligibility; safety considerations and referral in screening.

curriculum.module: Module 4 — Preparation, Set and Setting, Safety Planning
curriculum.detail: Developing therapeutic rapport; informed consent; developing a safety plan.
Dosing strategies and subjective experience; challenging behaviours in administration sessions; traumatic stress, de-escalation and safety in administration sessions.
Integration modalities and resources; boundaries and group dynamics in group facilitation; providing individual care and navigating challenging experiences in group administration sessions.

Required for licensure in both Oregon and Colorado; 'an in-depth opportunity for trainees to facilitate a non-ordinary state of consciousness experience under the guidance of a qualified supervisor'. Naropa listed an Oregon option at the Cora Center in Portland and a Colorado option, both with dates and costs TBD, with registration prioritising in-state residents. Memoru now lists Practicum as an approved offering on the Colorado DORA register.

Colorado requires post-training consultation before licensure. DORA's current guidance sets this at 40 hours, of which 10 hours must focus on ethical issues arising in the trainee's course of work and the remainder a mix of case review and structured learning, all completed within two years of the Training Licence being issued. Memoru is registered with DORA as offering consultation.

curriculum.module: Colorado rule-set the 150 hours must cover
curriculum.detail: Facilitator Best Practices (5h); Ethics and Colorado Natural Medicine Rules and Regulations (25h); Relational Boundaries and Introduction to Physical Touch (10h); Physical and Mental Health and State (25h); Drug Effects, Contraindications and Interactions (5h); Introduction to Trauma-Informed Care (10h); Introduction to Suicide Risk (5h); Indigenous, Social and Cultural Considerations (10h); Screening (5h); Preparation (10h); Administration (10h); Integration (10h); Group Facilitation (10h); Facilitator Development and Self-Care (10h). These are minimums; programmes may exceed them.

can: Actually lead to a real state licence — which almost nothing else in this field does. Complete the 150 didactic hours with a DORA-approved programme, 40 practicum hours and 40 consultation hours, hold current Basic Life Support certification, clear criminal-history screening, complete the Healthcare Professions Profile and pay the application fee, and Colorado will license you as a Natural Medicine Facilitator.

Legally administer psilocybin to adults in Colorado once licensed, and conduct preparation, administration and integration sessions — the three components of natural medicine services — for participants whose safety screen does not indicate the need for a medical or behavioural health provider.

Be completed by a Californian. There is no Colorado residency requirement for the Facilitator tier: eligibility is 21+, high school diploma or equivalent, US resident. The didactic phase is delivered live online, so the travel burden is the practicum and any in-person retreats.

Be stacked onto a Colorado clinical licence for the Clinical Facilitator tier, which uniquely allows you to practise your secondary profession simultaneously while providing natural medicine services. A California LMFT would first need Colorado LMFT licensure.

Be reached by endorsement from Oregon: Colorado grants Clinical Facilitator licensure by endorsement to applicants who hold a valid Colorado licence in their secondary field plus an Oregon facilitator licence held in good standing for one year.

Give you a real, current grounding in the operational parts of the job — screening, informed consent, safety planning, dosing, de-escalation, group work — which generic 'psychedelic-assisted therapy' certificates skip.
cannot: Do anything for you in California. A Colorado facilitator licence has no effect on a California BBS licence or scope, and psilocybin remains Schedule I federally and unlawful for therapeutic use in California. California has no regulated access programme: SB 58 was vetoed in October 2023, and the 2025-26 bills (AB 1103, SB 751, SB 1224, AB 2489) are research-funding and study measures.

Be obtained from Naropa University. Naropa transferred the programme to the independent Memoru Center in December 2024 and does not appear on Colorado DORA's approved-programme list. The Naropa web page describing this programme has not been updated since late 2024.

Qualify you for Oregon. Neither Naropa nor Memoru appears on Oregon Psilocybin Services' list of training programmes with approved curriculum as of 6 August 2026, despite the Naropa page's Oregon claims and a December 2024 statement that the Oregon transfer was 'in process'. Memoru's current training page claims Colorado only.

Let you do psychotherapy inside the psilocybin work, if you hold only the plain Facilitator licence. DORA is explicit: 'A facilitator cannot engage in psychotherapy, the practice of medicine, or any secondary profession that would require the use of touch beyond the scope allowed by 4 CCR 755-1 6.6, Supportive Touch.'
Be practised remotely. Licensed facilitation happens in Colorado, in person, under Colorado's regulatory structure — which means relocating, commuting, or building a bi-state practice.
Be budgeted for yet, because no tuition figure is published for the didactic programme, the practicum or the consultation, and DORA does not publish its licence fee schedule on the public site.
scope.disclaimer_quote: Psilocybin facilitation under the state regulatory adult use model is an emergent and evolving field. Naropa's non-degree PFT certificate program is designed to prepare facilitators for licensure in Colorado and Oregon. Because regulations vary state by state, additional training may be required for credentialing depending on the legal context of the facilitator's intended practice location. The future trajectory and guidelines for psilocybin facilitation vary by region, regulatory agency, and protocol, and are subject to changes in federal, state, and local guidelines.

Sara Gael Beauregard — Memoru co-founder; Boulder-based therapist and psychedelic researcher.

Syre Saniyah, PhD, LP — guest instructor; co-founder and Director of Programming of the Cora Center, a queer- and BIPOC-led psilocybin service centre in Portland, OR; holds an OHA-approved psilocybin facilitation certificate from Alma Institute. Fronts Memoru's 2026 info sessions.

pacifica-psychedelic.name: Psychedelics and Depth Psychology certificate series (Level 1 introductory; Advanced Level 2)
pacifica-psychedelic.location: Carpinteria / Santa Barbara, CA — delivered entirely online via Zoom
pacifica-psychedelic.one_line: Not a facilitator training — a pair of $1,095 online CE lecture courses on psychedelics through a depth-psychology lens, with a strong faculty roster, no practicum, and no state approval anywhere.
summary: Pacifica does have psychedelic-specific programmes, but they are continuing-education courses, not a facilitator credential, and it is important not to confuse the two. They live in Pacifica Extension — the institute's non-degree arm — as a two-level series called 'Psychedelics and Depth Psychology'. Level 1, 'Treatment and Transformation in an Animated Cosmos', ran 16 weeks (May-August 2025) for 14 CE credits. Level 2, the 'Advanced Psychedelics Graduate Certificate', ran 12 weeks (September-December 2025) for 10 CE credits. Both are $1,095 at the general rate, both are delivered as a weekly pre-recorded lecture plus a two-hour live Zoom discussion, and Level 1 is explicitly not a prerequisite for Level 2. Despite the words 'Graduate Certificate' in the title these are non-credit Extension offerings — the course page says so bluntly: 'This Certificate neither requires nor confers a license or degree.'

What you actually get is a very good reading list and unusual access to people who built the field. The Level 2 faculty includes Michael Mithoefer, MD, who ran the first MAPS Phase 2 MDMA trial and supervised therapists on the Phase 3 trials; Rosalind Watts, PhD, former clinical lead of the Imperial College psilocybin-for-depression trial and author of the ACE/ACER integration models; Saj Razvi, a former MAPS Phase 2 clinical researcher and co-developer of Psychedelic Somatic Interactional Psychotherapy; Neil Hanon, MD, who leads Grof Legacy Training in Canada; Jungian analyst Linda Carter on ketamine as an adjunct to analytic work; and psychiatrist Brian Stafford, MD, MPH, who anchors both levels. Level 1 added Robin Carhart-Harris, Bill Richards, Janis Phelps (founder of the CIIS programme), Bia Labate and Michael Winkelman. The framing throughout is depth-psychological and mythopoetic — Jung, Grof, Hillman-adjacent language, IFS, ecopsychology — rather than protocol-and-checklist clinical training.

For a California licensee the practical value is narrow but real and cheap. Pacifica is an approved CE sponsor for the California Board of Behavioral Sciences via CAMFT (provider #60721), so the 10 or 14 hours count toward LMFT, LCSW, LPCC and LEP renewal, and separately for psychologists through the California Psychological Association (PAC014) and for RNs (CEP 7177). CE credit costs an extra $30 and requires attendance at every live Zoom session — recordings alone earn the certificate of completion but not the CE hours. Discounts exist: $930.75 for Pacifica alumni and seniors, $876 for Lifelong Learner members, $657 for Pacifica Extension students on Level 1, with a 50% deposit option, instalments, and a limited scholarship pool.

The honest headline is that Pacifica runs retreats, short courses and CE certificates rather than a facilitator training credential, and that it has never sought or held state approval to train psilocybin facilitators. There is no practicum, no supervised client contact, no consultation hours, no admissions screening beyond payment, and nothing that any regulator recognises. There is also nothing currently scheduled: as of 6 August 2026 the Level 2 course is listed with dates 'TBD' under Coming Soon on Pacifica Extension's programme index, and Level 1 sits under 'Previous Programs'. Earlier one-off offerings — the eight-week 'Sacred Medicine and the Psyche' (2021, $595-$895, run with the Institute of Transpersonal and Archetypal Studies) and the two-day 'Psychedelia' film symposium (2021, co-sponsored by Chacruna, Fluence and MAPS) — are likewise archived. Note also that Pacifica's retreat site, retreat.pacifica.edu, now redirects to the Extension site; there is no separate psychedelic retreat programme.

cost.note: $1,095 general rate for each level, taken separately. $930.75 Pacifica alumni and senior rate; $876 Lifelong Learner member rate; $657 Pacifica Extension student rate (published on Level 1). Continuing education credits are an additional $30. A 50% deposit at registration with instalments is available, and a limited scholarship / reduced-tuition pool exists with a stated application deadline before each cohort. Cancellation: full refund 14+ days before start, 50% from 14 to 7 days, none inside 7 days. Prices are the ones published for the 2025 runs; no 2026 pricing has been posted.

pacifica-psychedelic.length: Level 1: 16 weeks (described as a four-month course). Level 2: 12 weeks (described as a three-month course).
pacifica-psychedelic.hours: Level 1: 14 CE credits, 16 live two-hour sessions plus recorded presentations and readings. Level 2: 10 CE credits, 11 live two-hour webinar sessions (12 scheduled weeks, one reading-only week) plus 12 recorded video sessions. No practicum, no supervised contact hours, no consultation hours.
pacifica-psychedelic.format: Fully online. Each week a pre-recorded lecture to watch at your own pace, followed by a live two-hour Zoom session with a faculty member and fellow students at 4:30-6:30pm PT (occasionally 8:30-10:30am PT for internationally based faculty). Course materials on the D2L platform, plus a private online discussion forum and a learning resource guide. All live sessions are recorded; watching recordings and keeping up with the forum earns the certificate of completion, but CE credits require live attendance at every session.
pacifica-psychedelic.eligibility: Open enrolment — no licence, degree, prerequisite or application required. The course page states the material is 'open to everyone' and names its intended audiences as Level 1 alumni and experienced practitioners; scholars, educators and researchers; mental health professionals (therapists, psychologists, social workers, counsellors); medical professionals and prescribers (MDs, RNs, NPs); and psychedelic facilitators, coaches and ceremonialists. Level 1 is explicitly not a prerequisite for Level 2.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 1 — Orientation to Level 2 Psychedelics Certificate
curriculum.detail: Overview and orientation, cohort formation into 'home pods'. Brian Stafford, MD, MPH and Katie Stone.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 2 — A History & Orientation to Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy and Models
curriculum.detail: History of psychotherapy and evidence-based therapies; evolution of psychedelic-assisted therapy theory, approach and research; comparison of psychedelic and non-psychedelic frames; and explicitly 'the challenges of getting psychedelic assisted therapy approved by the FDA and the consequences of its rejection'. Brian Stafford.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 3 — Psychedelic Healing through a Mythopoetic Lens: Depth Psychology and the Descent to Soul
curriculum.detail: Archetypal and initiatory themes, shadow integration, ancestral healing and cultural repair in psychedelic work. Simon Yugler, author of 'Psychedelics and the Soul'.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 4 — Pathways of Regeneration: MDMA and psilocybin in treating mental health challenges
curriculum.detail: A biopsychosocial, ecosystemic model combining low-to-moderate doses of MDMA and psilocybin; two case studies; the psychedelic landscape in South Africa. Mama Mycelia (Megan Hardy and Kate Ferguson).

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 5 — Ketamine as Adjunct to Clinical Depth Psychology: 'The Combination Method'
curriculum.detail: Case-study work on ketamine infusions alongside analytic treatment for depression, dissociation and suicidal ideation, and using active imagination afterward for integration. Jungian analyst Linda Carter, MSN, CS, IAAP. The most directly applicable session for a California clinician, since ketamine is the only modality legally available here.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 6 — A Grofian approach to holotropic states of consciousness
curriculum.detail: Grof's cartography of the psyche, COEX systems, unfinished gestalts, spiritual emergence; directive versus facilitating approaches. Neil Hanon, MD, who leads Grof Breathwork and Psychedelic Therapy training streams in Canada.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 7 — Internal Family Systems and MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD
curriculum.detail: The therapeutic method used in the MDMA clinical trials, spontaneous parts-work under MDMA, and unpublished sub-study data. Michael Mithoefer, MD, who ran the first MAPS Phase 2 trial and supervised Phase 3 therapists.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 8 — Psychedelic Somatic Interactional Psychotherapy (PSIP)
curriculum.detail: Autonomic nervous system states, traumatic transference, and selective inhibition; an actively relational alternative to the sitter model. Saj Razvi, former MAPS Phase 2 clinical researcher.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 9 — Creating Islands of Connectedness: the ACER Integration model
curriculum.detail: Accept, Connect, Embody, Restore; theoretical grounding in ACT, ecotherapy, liberation psychology and peer-led care, plus a critical look at the limits of online mutual-aid communities. Rosalind Watts, PhD.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 10 — The role of music in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy
curriculum.detail: Reading and viewing only, no live meeting (US Thanksgiving week).

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 11 — The Nature-Based Map of the Human Psyche and Wild Mind Way of Psychedelic Facilitation
curriculum.detail: Eco-depth work of the Animas Valley Institute; adaptations for preparation, journeying and integration. Brian Stafford.

curriculum.module: Level 2, Week 12 — Integration of the psychedelic-assisted therapy models and approaches
curriculum.detail: Small and large group synthesis of the twelve weeks. Brian Stafford and Katie Stone.

curriculum.module: Level 1 (16 weeks) — Psychedelics and Depth Psychology: Treatment and Transformation in an Animated Cosmos
curriculum.detail: Survey course covering current and historical use of plant-based medicines in Western societies; use and challenges in Indigenous cultures; the worldview underlying modern medicine and psychiatry; the history and status of clinical research; animistic and shamanistic worldviews; biopharmacology; micro, suitable and heroic dosing; the qualities, skills, ethics and training to look for in a psychedelic-assisted therapist, ceremonialist or sitter; set and setting; contraindications, supporting challenging journeys and harm reduction; and the legal history and status of these medicines in the US and worldwide. 14 CECs. Last run 7 May - 20 August 2025.

can: Bank 10 or 14 hours of California BBS-qualifying continuing education toward LMFT, LCSW, LPCC or LEP renewal for an extra $30 on top of tuition — Pacifica is a CAMFT-approved CE provider, #60721 (and CPA PAC014 for psychologists, BRN CEP 7177 for nurses).
Get a genuinely well-taught theoretical grounding in psychedelic-assisted therapy models from people who ran the pivotal trials, without pretending it is clinical training.
Do better preparation and integration work with California clients, which is legal psychotherapy and requires no special credential of any kind.

Bring depth-psychological, Grofian, IFS and somatic framing to ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in California — the only psychedelic modality a California therapist can practise today, and one where the therapist provides the psychotherapy while a physician, NP or PA handles the prescribing.
Add a recognisable, low-cost line to a CV while deciding whether a $10,000-plus facilitator training is worth it.
cannot: Change your licence or scope of practice in any way. Pacifica states it directly: 'This Certificate neither requires nor confers a license or degree.' The California BBS neither recognises nor requires it.

Qualify you to facilitate psilocybin anywhere. Pacifica is not on the Oregon Health Authority's list of programmes with approved curriculum, nor on Colorado DORA's list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs — both checked 6 August 2026.

Give you any supervised client contact. There is no practicum, no consultation hours, no case supervision and no skills assessment — only lectures, readings, a discussion forum and live Zoom seminars.
Let you administer psilocybin or MDMA to anyone in California. Both remain Schedule I federally and California has no regulated access programme.

Screen you for suitability. Enrolment is open to anyone who pays, including people with no clinical licence at all, which is a real difference from the admissions-gated programmes at Berkeley or CIIS and should factor into how a hiring clinic reads it.
scope.disclaimer_quote: Because of the availability, power, and growing legalization of these medicines for clinical, ceremonial, and recreational uses, these ideas and conversations around psychedelics are open to everyone. This Certificate neither requires nor confers a license or degree.

faculty: Brian Stafford, MD, MPH — anchors both levels; triple-board-trained psychiatrist, former Anschutz Family Chair in Early Childhood Psychiatry, completed the CIIS/MAPS psychedelic-assisted therapy programme, now a Senior Guide and trainer at the Animas Valley Institute. He teaches psychedelics at Pacifica and facilitates preparation, journeying and integration privately.
Michael Mithoefer, MD — ran the first MAPS-sponsored Phase 2 MDMA trial for PTSD with Annie Mithoefer, and supervised therapists on the Phase 3 trials. The single biggest name on the roster.
Rosalind Watts, PhD — former clinical lead of the psilocybin-for-depression trial at Imperial College London; created the ACE/ACER integration models and the Watts Connectedness Scale.

Saj Razvi — founder and Director of Education at the Psychedelic Somatic Institute, former MAPS Phase 2 clinical researcher, co-developer of PSIP; teaches clinicians to work legally with ketamine and cannabis in private practice.

Neil Hanon, MD, FRCPC — Canadian psychiatrist, certified Holotropic Breathwork facilitator, co-founder of Jamaica Grief Retreats, former Medical Director of TheraPsil; since 2023 leads Grof Legacy Training's Canadian Breathwork and Psychedelic Therapy streams.
Linda Carter, MSN, CS, IAAP — Jungian analyst in Carpinteria, 45+ years in practice, on ketamine as an adjunct to analytic treatment.
Simon Yugler — depth-psychology MA from Pacifica, author of 'Psychedelics and the Soul'; has taught for five facilitator training programmes including CIIS, Naropa and InnerTrek.
Katie Stone — co-facilitator of the Level 2 orientation and closing sessions.

polaris-insight-kap.name: Polaris/Rainfall Certificate of Training in Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy
polaris-insight-kap.location: San Francisco, CA — live-online modules plus five-day in-person practicum retreats (2026 retreats in Berkeley, CA and Portland, OR)
polaris-insight-kap.one_line: Modular, à-la-carte KAP training from a San Francisco clinic that has been doing this since 2018 — you can start for $375, get a usable foundation for $1,950, and only commit to the full 1–2 year certificate if you want it.
summary: Polaris Insight Center opened in 2018 as one of the first ketamine-assisted psychotherapy clinics, started training clinicians in 2020, and now says it has trained over 2,000. Its founders are MAPS-trained clinicians who worked in Phase 2 and Phase 3 MDMA-assisted psychotherapy trials for PTSD, and the lead trainers studied with the Ketamine Training Center and KRIYA Institute. That lineage matters mainly because it explains the house style: transpersonal, inner-directed, psychedelic-therapy-flavoured rather than protocol-and-checklist medical.

The structure is deliberately modular rather than a single tuition bill. Everything is priced per unit: each full-day (8-hour) module is $375 ($350 plus a $25 non-refundable admin fee), with 8 CE credits available for an extra $79. Module 1, 'Introduction to Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy', is the prerequisite for Modules 2–5 and the Practice Module. Buying all six as the Foundational Series is $1,950, a $300 discount. An alternative on-ramp is the 2026 Cohort — 52 training hours over five months (12 three-hour sessions, a Training & Practice Module, and four discussion groups) starting 11 September 2026 for $2,450, with 44 CE hours available for a flat $350. The cohort covers the same content as Modules 1–5 but in a fixed group, and its discussion groups count for 3 of the 12 group-consultation hours the certificate requires.

The certificate itself is the real commitment and Polaris is honest that it is 'expected to be a 1-to-2-year process.' It requires: Modules 1–5 plus the Practice Module; any two of nine advanced or special-topic modules; 12 group consultation sessions AND 12 individual consultation sessions, with letters of recommendation from both consultants; one five-day experiential practicum retreat (or an approved alternative such as Grof Transpersonal Training or holotropic breathwork intensives); a minimum of 18 real KAP sessions with at least three different clients; a 3–5 page reflection essay; and an administrative processing fee. That clinical-hours requirement is the thing to plan around: you cannot finish this certificate without already having a working KAP practice, which means you must have solved the prescriber problem first.

The experiential practicum retreat is where trainees have their own ketamine sessions. Polaris does not say so in one blunt sentence, but the retreat page promises you will 'learn through direct experience about the medical, biological, psychological, transpersonal, and phenomenological aspects of the ketamine experience,' screens applicants for medical contraindications (sleep apnea, untreated blood pressure or heart conditions, history of psychosis, stroke risk, active mania, recent TBI, untreated seizure disorders), and is run in collaboration with a medical clinic, Rainfall Medicine. Trainee testimonials on Polaris's own site refer to 'my own journey content' and to 'sitting with someone experiencing a journey.' The retreat price is not published anywhere on the site, which is the single biggest hole in an otherwise transparent price list.
modality: General/substance-agnostic (non-ordinary states of consciousness, holotropic breathwork as an approved experiential alternative)

can: Practise ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in California today, as the psychotherapy half of a collaborative pair — because ketamine is an FDA-approved anaesthetic that a licensed prescriber can prescribe off-label, this is the one psychedelic-assisted modality a California LMFT/LCSW/LPCC/psychologist can actually do now.

Earn CE hours that count toward California licence renewal. Polaris states verbatim: 'Polaris Insight Center is approved by the American Psychological Association to sponsor continuing education for psychologists... The California Board of Behavioral Sciences accepts CE credits for LCSW, LPCC, LEP, and LMFT license renewal for programs offered by approved sponsors of CE by the American Psychological Association.' 8 CE per full-day module ($79), 44 CE for the cohort ($350). Note: not CME, so physicians must check their own board.
Be listed in the Polaris/Rainfall KAP Practitioner Directory on completing the certificate — a marketing and referral asset, not a credential.

Present a training credential that KAP platforms and clinics actually recognise: Journey Clinical lists Polaris among the didactic trainings it accepts for onboarding (alongside CIIS, MAPS, Fluence, Alchemy and others).

Do preparation and integration work with clients around psychedelic experiences that occur outside your office — legal in California with no special credential, and something the Integration and Ethics modules address directly.
cannot: Prescribe, dispense, possess, or administer ketamine. You are not a prescriber. In the standard KAP arrangement an MD, DO, NP or PA holds all medical authority — clearance, dosing, prescribing, monitoring — and the therapist leads psychotherapy only. Journey Clinical puts the boundary plainly: 'Strict adherence to scope of practice is essential — psychotherapists should never engage in activities that could be interpreted as practicing medicine or psychiatry.'

Touch psilocybin, MDMA or LSD. Psilocybin and LSD are Schedule I in California under Health & Safety Code §11054; MDMA-assisted therapy is still investigational and not FDA-approved (Lykos Therapeutics, whose expanded-access programme is fully enrolled and closed, describes itself as still 'focused on pursuing FDA approval').

Qualify for Oregon psilocybin facilitator licensure. Polaris Insight Center does not appear on Oregon Psilocybin Services' list of Current Active Psilocybin Training Programs (15 programs; checked 2026-08-06).
Qualify for Colorado natural-medicine facilitator licensure. Polaris does not appear on Colorado DORA's Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs list (checked 2026-08-06).

Change your BBS licence, title, or scope. The certificate is a credential from a private clinic; the BBS neither recognises nor requires it, and nothing about the training expands what your licence permits.
Finish the certificate without a live KAP caseload. The 18-sessions-with-3-clients requirement means you must already have a prescriber partner and paying clients before you can complete it.

summary: PRATI is a Colorado 501(c)(3) founded in 2019 out of the Wholeness Center in Fort Collins by psychiatrist Scott Shannon and colleagues. Its flagship course, Foundations in Psychedelic Medicine, is a four-day in-person retreat at Sunrise Ranch in Loveland, Colorado, capped at 32 participants for the September 3–6, 2026 cohort. It is explicitly built around ketamine: PRATI's own framing is that “ketamine is currently the only legal and widely used psychedelic in the U.S.” and is therefore the entry point for the rest of the field. Trainees must stay on site for the whole program; family and friends are not permitted at the venue.

The distinguishing feature — and the reason clinicians talk about PRATI — is the experiential component. On days two and three, trainees work in dyads and may receive ketamine themselves by two routes, intramuscular and sublingual. This is legal because ketamine is a Schedule III FDA-approved anaesthetic (21 CFR § 1308.13(c)(7)) administered here by a contracted medical provider, Evolve Mind Wellness, whose psychiatric director German Ascani, MD also serves as PRATI's medical/psychiatric director. Participation is optional, requires a pre-training virtual medical evaluation, requires a four-hour fast, and costs a separate $330 paid directly to Evolve Mind Wellness (prorated to $130–$280 for scholarship recipients). PRATI states plainly that the training “remains fully valuable and complete” for anyone not medically cleared or not wishing to participate, and that non-medicine “inner journey” experiences are available instead.

Eligibility is open to LMFTs. PRATI requires an active licence in good standing in a medical or mental-health field — provisional licences are accepted — plus at least 1,000 hours of direct clinical service. It is not prescriber-only: acupuncturists, chaplains, chiropractors, end-of-life doulas, naturopaths, nurses and physical therapists are also listed as eligible. Massage therapists are explicitly excluded. Pricing is two-tier: $3,000 for all non-physician participants, $4,450 for MDs and DOs, with a $500 non-refundable deposit. Lodging and meals at Sunrise Ranch are booked and paid separately, by the bed, and are not included at any price tier. Partial scholarships exist in three tiers ($500 / $1,650 / $2,475 paid to PRATI) across five equity categories.

Two things a buyer should weigh. First, PRATI is not accredited to award continuing-education credit: on request it will issue “a statement and summary of training hours (approximately 20),” which means a California LMFT gets no BBS-countable CE from a $3,000 course. Second, it confers no regulatory standing. PRATI does not appear on Colorado DORA's list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs, and its own separate psilocybin practicum requires that you have already completed a Colorado-approved facilitator training somewhere else and hold a Natural Medicine facilitator training licence. PRATI also runs an End of Life / Existential Distress psychedelic-assisted therapy training, a Business of Psychedelic Medicine course, KAP consultation groups and international “Embracing the Sacred” psilocybin immersions in Mexico; those are separate purchases.

prati.eligibility: Open to LMFTs and other licensed clinicians — not prescriber-only. Two hard requirements: (1) an active professional licence in good standing in a medical or mental-health-related field, with provisional licences (e.g. PLPC, LPCC) accepted, and chaplains and end-of-life doulas qualifying with proof of certification; and (2) at least 1,000 hours of direct experience providing clinical services. Also eligible: acupuncturists/East Asian medicine practitioners, chaplains, chiropractors, end-of-life doulas, naturopathic doctors, nurses, physical therapists. Massage therapists are explicitly not eligible. Registrations from ineligible individuals may be cancelled and deposits forfeited.

curriculum.detail: “Two optional ketamine experiences (intramuscular and sublingual) contingent on medical approval and supported by a fellow trainee.” Held on days two and three, in dyads, after a pre-training virtual medical evaluation by PRATI's contracted medical provider and a minimum four-hour fast.
“Harm reduction and ethical practices in psychedelic medicine.”
“Preparation and integration strategies for psychedelic experiences.”
“Guiding clients through nonordinary states of consciousness” and “facilitating transformative sessions using effective tools and techniques.”
“The role of music and playlist creation in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy.” Course director Stephen Thomas, LCSW curates PRATI's KAP playlists.
“Clinical care for severely depressed and suicidal individuals.”
“Ketamine dosing and administration best practices, including various routes of delivery.” Note this is taught to a mixed room; it does not give a non-prescribing therapist authority to dose anyone.
“Exploration of set and setting, ceremony, and ritual in psychedelic medicine.”
“Perspectives on worldview and systemic change within the psychedelic paradigm.” PRATI describes its purpose as “restoring connection to the sacred” and weaves that framing through the course.

can: Work as the therapist on a ketamine-assisted psychotherapy team in California. That is legal for an LMFT today — but it is your BBS licence, not the PRATI certificate, that authorises the psychotherapy. Ketamine is Schedule III and FDA-approved as an anaesthetic (21 CFR § 1308.13(c)(7)); it is prescribed off-label by a physician, NP or PA, not by you.

Do preparation and integration work with clients who are receiving ketamine from a prescriber, or who have had psychedelic experiences elsewhere. No special credential is needed for integration work by a licensed therapist.

Say truthfully that you have had two legal, medically supervised ketamine experiences yourself, by two routes of administration, and have sat for a peer during theirs. Very few US trainings offer that legally, and it is the single thing this course provides that reading and CE webinars cannot.
Be more credible to a ketamine clinic or group practice that is hiring therapists — PRATI has run these since 2019 and has name recognition among KAP clinicians.
Create a free profile in PRATI's public directory of practitioners and join the alumni listserv after completing a training.
Build a base you could later extend: PRATI's own psilocybin practicum, its End of Life / Existential Distress training, and its KAP consultation groups are separate purchases layered on top.
cannot: Cannot prescribe, obtain, possess or administer ketamine. An LMFT has no prescriptive authority in California and this course does not create any. In the training itself the ketamine is administered by a contracted medical provider, not by trainees.

Cannot legally use psilocybin or MDMA with clients in California. Both remain Schedule I federally (21 CFR § 1308.11(d)), California has no state-regulated psilocybin or MDMA programme as of August 2026, and FDA has not approved MDMA-assisted therapy since the August 2024 complete response letter to Lykos.

Cannot practise as a licensed facilitator in Colorado on the strength of this course. PRATI does not appear on DORA's published list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs, and PRATI's own psilocybin practicum page states that participants “must have successfully completed a Colorado-approved Psilocybin Facilitator Training Program before enrolling” and must already hold a Natural Medicine facilitator training licence.

Cannot use it toward Oregon psilocybin facilitator licensure. Oregon only recognises training programmes whose curriculum has been approved by Oregon Psilocybin Services under ORS 475A; PRATI does not claim OPS curriculum approval anywhere on its site, and its FAQ says its training “does not fulfill all the requirements to become a licensed facilitator in these states.”
Cannot count it as continuing education. PRATI states it is “not accredited to offer CEUs.” A California LMFT gets zero BBS-countable CE hours for $3,000 plus lodging.

Does not change your licence, title, or scope of practice in any way the California BBS recognises. There is no BBS endorsement, registration or specialty designation for psychedelic-assisted therapy.
scope.disclaimer_quote: The field of psychedelic medicine is rapidly evolving, and ketamine is currently the only legal psychedelic that can be used in clinical practice across all U.S. states. At this time, there is no standardized national certification process required to practice ketamine-assisted psychotherapy. Some states, like Colorado and Oregon, are developing regulated models for legal access to other psychedelics, such as psilocybin. While PRATI’s training may contribute to the knowledge and skills required for psychedelic therapy, it does not fulfill all the requirements to become a licensed facilitator in these states. However, it may meet certain prerequisite components of the licensing process.

faculty: Scott Shannon, MD — founder; child psychiatrist and founder of the Wholeness Center in Fort Collins, the clinic PRATI grew out of after its involvement in Phase III MDMA research.

Stephen Thomas, LCSW — Foundations in Psychedelic Medicine Training Director; Fort Collins psychotherapist and KAP practitioner, board member of the Nowak Society, and the person who curates PRATI's KAP music playlists.

German Ascani, MD, MS — PRATI's lead psychiatric consultant and medical/psychiatric director for the trainings; the medical provider behind the experiential component through his practice Evolve Mind Wellness. Board-certified psychiatrist, former MAPS/Lykos associate consultant and Phase 3 MDMA study therapist, and a licensed Colorado natural medicine clinical facilitator.
Christine (Chris) Pateros, MA, RN — founding team member, End of Life PAT Training Director and lead faculty; Ketamine Training Center-trained (2019) and MAPS MDMA-trained (2024).
Jason Sienknecht, LPC, CAS — founding team member who led early curriculum development.
Wilhelmina De Castro, LCSW — Executive Director.

Board of directors includes Janis Phelps, PhD (founder of the CIIS psychedelic therapy certificate), Andrew Weil, MD, Joe Tafur, MD, Lia Mix, MS, MFT and Kwasi Adusei, DNP, PMHNP-BC — a useful signal of who vouches for the organisation.

voices.text: PRATI's own FAQ is unusually blunt for the sector: “Will I be certified to practice KAP or psychedelic medicine after the training?” is answered with, in effect, no — there is no national certification, and the training “does not fulfill all the requirements to become a licensed facilitator” in Colorado or Oregon. Read that before you read any of the endorsements.
voices.who: PRATI Foundations training FAQ, verified August 2026

voices.text: “Currently, PRATI is not accredited to offer CEUs for our training programs. However, upon request, we can provide participants with a statement and summary of training hours (approximately 20).” For a California LMFT that means $3,000 plus lodging buys zero BBS-countable continuing education.
voices.who: PRATI Foundations training FAQ, verified August 2026

voices.text: A peer-reviewed risk-benefit analysis of experiential training — the thing PRATI is best known for — concludes it “should not be mandatory,” flagging physical and psychological risk, dual relationships, privacy and confidentiality, equity of access, and undue pressure to participate. PRATI's version is optional, medically screened and priced separately, which addresses several of those objections but not the dual-relationship and privacy ones: you take the medicine alongside colleagues, supported by a fellow trainee.
voices.who: Rosenbaum et al., “Experiential Training in Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy: A Risk-Benefit Analysis,” The Hastings Center Report, July 2024

voices.text: A companion analysis in International Review of Psychiatry reaches a similar verdict: “the current evidence does not justify making personal psychedelic(-like) experience a requirement for psychedelic therapists,” though it should be available to those who want it. In other words, the thing you are mainly paying PRATI for is valuable but not evidence-established as necessary to competence.
voices.who: Villiger, International Review of Psychiatry, December 2024

voices.text: Cautionary context for any five-figure or four-figure psychedelic training purchase: when Synthesis Institute collapsed in 2023 it left roughly 230 students across four cohorts of a $12,997 programme in limbo, mid-course, with company liabilities around $850,000 and an unclear path to refunds. Unaccredited training companies are not schools with tuition-protection obligations by default. PRATI is a long-running nonprofit rather than a VC-funded startup, and its course is four days rather than thirteen months, which limits the exposure — but its deposit is non-refundable and non-transferable, and cancellation inside two weeks forfeits the full cost.
voices.who: Psychedelic Alpha, “Inside Synthesis Institute’s Implosion,” March 2023

voices.text: “I am leaving the training feeling inspired and knowledgeable to start offering KAP. But even more important, I feel transformed on a personal level by the experientials and the deep connections I made.” Note this and the other endorsements are testimonials selected and published by PRATI on its own sales page, not independent reviews.
voices.who: Lauren Going, LCSW-C, endorsement published by PRATI

voices.text: Absence check, done directly rather than taken on trust: PRATI does not appear on Colorado DORA's published list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs (which as of August 2026 lists Academy of Intrinsic Studies, Acadia Professional Learning, Bodhi Academy, Center for Medicinal Mindfulness, Ceremonia Edu, Changa Institute, CU CPR, Elemental Psychedelics, Entheogen Institute, Fluence, InnerTrek, Memoru Center, Numinus, SoundMind Institute and The Resurgence Training Institute). PRATI's role in the Colorado system is downstream: it sells a supervised psilocybin practicum to people who trained elsewhere.
voices.who: Colorado DORA Division of Professions and Occupations, Natural Medicine programme page, verified 6 August 2026

prati.status_2026: Enrolling. Registration is open for the September 3–6, 2026 cohort at Sunrise Ranch, capped at 32 participants; the scholarship application deadline was 27 July 2026 and full payment was due the same date. Verified 6 August 2026 on PRATI's event page.

video.title: PRATI Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy Training Experience
video.who: Psychedelic Research and Training Institute (PRATI) official YouTube channel
video.why: PRATI's own footage of the retreat format — the venue, the dyad work and the room — which is the part of the purchase that is hardest to judge from a web page. Treat it as marketing, but it is accurate marketing about what four days there look like.

gaps: No published hour-by-hour schedule or syllabus; the “approximately 20 hours” figure comes only from the CE answer in the FAQ.

Sunrise Ranch lodging and meal prices are only reachable through an off-site link, so the true all-in cost of attending could not be pinned down. Budget for four to five nights of lodging plus flights on top of the $3,000/$4,450.
No CME is advertised for physicians and PRATI does not say whether it intends to seek accreditation.
PRATI says it has “hundreds of alumni” since 2019 but publishes no cohort-by-cohort numbers, completion rates or outcome data.

No independent journalism about PRATI specifically was found — the criticism cited here is field-level (experiential-training ethics, unaccredited training-company risk), not program-specific. Every positive quote about PRATI that could be located is a testimonial PRATI itself published.

Oregon Psilocybin Services now publishes its approved-curriculum list through a JavaScript application that could not be enumerated from this environment; the “not Oregon-approved” finding rests on PRATI's own FAQ statement and the absence of any Oregon claim on its site rather than on reading the OHA list line by line.
It is not stated whether the ketamine experiential creates any patient record with Evolve Mind Wellness, or how that interacts with a trainee's own medical history and future disclosure obligations.

psychedelic-coalition-for-health.name: Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy & Integration Training
psychedelic-coalition-for-health.location: Los Angeles, CA — residential training week at a retreat centre in Topanga Canyon, bookended by two virtual cohort meetings
psychedelic-coalition-for-health.one_line: A short, expensive, residential Los Angeles training built around actually taking ketamine yourself and sitting for a peer — deliberately unhurried, APA-sponsored CE that counts for a California LMFT, and, as of August 2026, apparently dormant: applications closed, dates TBA, site copyright 2022.
summary: PCH is the smallest and most concentrated of these three. It is not a year-long curriculum; it is a residential training week in Topanga Canyon in Los Angeles with a virtual cohort meeting before and after. The premise is experiential: 'Experiential sessions with ketamine will allow participants to practice ketamine-assisted therapy and become effective facilitators in integration.' Each participant gets time as the person in the non-ordinary state and time as the person holding the space. PCH describes its pacing as the point: 'Our ethos is slow and spacious'; 'We are shifting out of the traditional model of speed and hyper-productivity in favor of sustained, unhurried learning with lasting impact.'

The balance is roughly: clinical and pharmacological grounding (research history, current protocols, psychopharmacology, dosing and medical safety); core competencies (preparation, set and setting, facilitation, integration, plus transpersonal, IFS, somatic and ACT frames, and music playlist curation); direct ketamine experience with harm-reduction essentials; an integration block the programme treats as its distinguishing emphasis, listed literally as 'Integration Integration Integration'; and a professional-development block covering practice management, legal and insurance issues, and ethics. There are master classes across ketamine, MDMA, psilocybin, ayahuasca, 5-MeO-DMT and ibogaine — education about substances the training does not, and cannot, license you to use.

Tuition is published, which is more than SoundMind does: $5,000 for mental health professionals, $6,000 for physicians, with a need-based, equity-informed scholarship. An earlier, still-visible block on the same page shows $4,000 / $5,000 / $1,500 scholarship for the October 2021 cohort. Tuition explicitly excludes accommodation, meals and CEs; the retreat centre costs a further $1,350–$2,100 for five nights all-inclusive with three meals a day, and accommodation is 'all but required'. The PCH Virtual Symposium is included and required. CE is up to 50 credits for the in-person training, sponsored by the Spiritual Competency Academy, which is APA-approved — and PCH states directly that 'The California Board of Behavioral Sciences accepts CE credits for LCSW, LPCC, LEP, and LMFT license renewal for programs offered by approved sponsors of CE by the American Psychological Association.' That checks out against the BBS's own list of recognised approval agencies.

The awkward part: as of 6 August 2026 the site says 'applications CLOSED', 'New cohort date TBD', shows 'DATE TBA' and 'DATE TBD' everywhere a date should be, and carries a 2022 copyright line in the footer. The only live-looking element is a merchandise link. PCH was founded by two Los Angeles clinicians, Lauren Taus, LCSW and Nicholas Brüss, EdD, LMFT — Brüss was a co-therapist on the MAPS Phase 3 MDMA trial in Los Angeles and has provided KAP since 2017 — and the training's design clearly reflects their own practices. But treat this as a paused programme unless you contact them and get a date.

cost.note: $5,000 for mental health professionals; $6,000 for physicians (an older block on the same page shows $4,000 / $5,000 and a $1,500 need-based, equity-informed scholarship rate for the October 2021 cohort). 'Tuition does not include accommodations, meals, or CEs.' The Topanga Canyon retreat centre costs a further $1,350–$2,100 for five nights, all-inclusive with three meals a day, and staying there is 'all but required'. The PCH Virtual Symposium is included in tuition; if you already paid for it separately, that payment is credited against tuition.

psychedelic-coalition-for-health.length: A residential training week in Los Angeles (five nights at the retreat centre), plus one live virtual cohort pre-meeting and one live virtual post-meeting. The October 2021 cohort ran as two four-day in-person weekends (7–10 October and 21–24 October) with a virtual post-meeting on 30 October; the current structure shown is a single training week, date TBD.
psychedelic-coalition-for-health.hours: Not published as a total. The nearest proxy is the CE figure: 50 CEs are available for the in-person training (the site footer says 'up to 60 CE' for mental health professionals — the two figures are not reconciled anywhere).
psychedelic-coalition-for-health.format: Residential and in-person, with virtual bookends. Two live virtual cohort meetings (opening and closing) plus a five-night stay at PCH's training retreat centre in Topanga Canyon, Los Angeles, with three farm-fresh meals a day, an outdoor sauna, cold plunge, hot tub, lap pool and outdoor showers on site. The PCH Virtual Symposium (recorded, 12+ hours of sessions) is included and required, though trainees may watch recordings rather than attend live.
psychedelic-coalition-for-health.eligibility: Open to LMFTs, and to pre-licensed therapists. 'This professional training requires applicants to have an advanced degree in either mental health or medicine.' The listed categories are: Marriage and Family Therapists (LMFT), Professional Clinical Counselors (LPC), Clinical Social Workers (LCSW), Clinical Psychologists (PhD/PsyD), Pre-licensed therapists (MA), Registered Nurses (BSN), Nurse Practitioners (NP), and Physicians (MD/DO). 'Early career mental health or medical professionals may apply and set up a discussion of your situation to evaluate whether this program fits for your level of experience.' Unlike SoundMind, this is not open to the general public.

curriculum.detail: History of psychedelic research; current psychedelic-assisted research protocols; psychopharmacology of psychoactive medicines; dosing protocols and medical safety.

Preparation, set and setting, facilitation and integration; foundational therapeutic principles including transpersonal, Internal Family Systems, somatic and ACT approaches; how to be with non-ordinary states of consciousness; music playlist development, rationale and curation.

curriculum.module: Direct Experience of Ketamine-assisted Therapy & Integration
curriculum.detail: Essentials of harm reduction; KAP preparation, set and setting, facilitation; 'Safe and legal experiences with ketamine'; 'Time and space to learn in a non-ordinary state of consciousness'. This is the experiential core — participants take ketamine and also practise sitting for others.

curriculum.module: Integration Integration Integration / Psychedelic-Informed Integrative and Collaborative Approach
curriculum.detail: Integrative tools for eliciting transformative experiences; medications and nutritional supplements for optimal mental health; maintaining lifestyle changes; mind-body practices to support integration. PCH describes integration as what makes its training unusual and builds schedule space around it.

Practice management issues — legal, insurance, safety; ethics in psychedelic-assisted therapy; community building and professional connections. The training also asks participants to 'Understand political and clinical controversies in the field'.

Ketamine, MDMA, Psilocybin, Ayahuasca, 5-MeO-DMT, Ibogaine — taught as education about the compounds and their contexts. Only the ketamine content maps onto anything a California clinician can practise.

can: Count up to 50 CE credits toward your California BBS renewal. This is the clearest concrete return. CE for psychologists is provided by the Spiritual Competency Academy, an APA-approved sponsor, and the BBS recognises APA as a CE approval agency for LMFT, LCSW, LPCC and LEP renewals (36 hours per two-year renewal period). PCH states the BBS-acceptance point on its own CE page.

Practise ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in California, in collaboration with a physician, NP or PA who prescribes. PCH is direct that this is the deliverable: 'We will prepare you to practice ketamine-assisted therapy, support you in building a team of professionals to work with.'

Work as a psychedelic integration specialist — PCH says the training 'builds competency and confidence to practice as a psychedelic integration specialist for clients'. Integration is ordinary psychotherapy and needs no credential.

Have had a legal, supervised ketamine experience yourself and practised sitting for a peer. Among these three programmes this is the most experientially front-loaded per dollar, and it is the one thing you genuinely cannot get from reading.

Be positioned for a future legal framework, which is how PCH frames the non-ketamine content: 'This training helps prepare you for working with MDMA and psilocybin in therapy when these consciousness tools are legally available.'

Be credible to a Los Angeles ketamine clinic. The founders are embedded in that scene — Nicholas Brüss is Clinical Director of Psychedelic Therapies at Hope Integrative Psychiatry and was a co-therapist on the MAPS Phase 3 MDMA trial in LA.
cannot: Change your licence or scope. It is a certificate of attendance plus CE hours; the BBS does not issue, require or recognise a psychedelic-therapy credential.
Qualify you for Oregon psilocybin facilitator licensure. PCH does not appear on OHA's live list of training programmes with approved curriculum (15 programmes, checked 6 August 2026).

Qualify you for Colorado natural medicine facilitator licensure. PCH does not appear on DORA's Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs list (checked 6 August 2026). Neither state is even mentioned on PCH's site.

Let you administer or prescribe ketamine. The prescribing and medical responsibility sits with a physician, NP or PA; PCH's model is explicitly team-based, 'support you in building a team of professionals to work with'.

Give you any access to psilocybin, MDMA, ayahuasca, 5-MeO-DMT or ibogaine in practice. The master classes on those are education. All remain Schedule I federally; California's SB 58 was vetoed in October 2023 and the state's 2025 action was a bill to accelerate study of psychedelics for PTSD, not to legalise therapeutic use. The FDA issued a complete response letter on MDMA-assisted therapy in August 2024 and it has not been approved since. PCH's own framing acknowledges the constraint: 'We support following the outcomes of validated research, and upholding the laws of the country in which you reside.'
Be relied on as currently available. As of 6 August 2026 applications are closed, all dates read TBD, and the site footer says © 2022.
scope.disclaimer_quote: The PCH training is designed for clinically licensed professionals to develop the core competencies necessary to provide psychedelic-assisted therapy and integration. We will prepare you to practice ketamine-assisted therapy, support you in building a team of professionals to work with to provide more integrative treatment for clients/patients, and a kinder relationship with work. This training helps prepare you for working with MDMA and psilocybin in therapy when these consciousness tools are legally available. This training also builds competency and confidence to practice as a psychedelic integration specialist for clients. We support following the outcomes of validated research, and upholding the laws of the country in which you reside.

faculty: Lauren Taus, LCSW — co-founder and lead trainer; Los Angeles psychotherapist; trained by MAPS for MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for complex PTSD and by Dr Phil Wolfson in Ketamine Assisted Psychotherapy; long background in trauma-sensitive yoga, studied with David Emerson under Bessel van der Kolk's supervision at the Trauma Institute in Boston.

Nicholas Brüss, EdD, LMFT — co-founder and lead trainer, and the reason this programme is legible to an LMFT reader: he holds the same licence. Trained as a psychedelic therapist by MAPS and served as a co-therapist on the MAPS-sponsored FDA Phase III MDMA-assisted therapy trial for PTSD in Los Angeles. Has provided KAP since 2017, certified IFS therapist since 2015, Clinical Director of Psychedelic Therapies at Hope Integrative Psychiatry, Zendo Project volunteer, Certified Mindfulness Facilitator through UCLA's MARC and a certified CCT teacher through Stanford's CCARE.
David Lukoff, PhD — named as the CE contact via the Spiritual Competency Academy, the APA-approved sponsor for the programme's psychologist CE.

PCH states the training is 'unique in its commitment to share with its participants a variety of techniques and perspectives by clinicians that use them', but does not publish a roster of guest faculty for the in-person training.

voices.text: Our ethos is slow and spacious to create sustained shift for the providers and the ones that they will serve. ... We are shifting out of the traditional model of speed and hyper-productivity in favor of sustained, unhurried learning with lasting impact.
voices.who: PCH, on its own training page — worth quoting because it is the clearest statement of what you are buying instead of hours

voices.text: Current and historic drug policies have targeted communities of color, leaving unfathomable consequences on the lives of many. PCH is committed to taking action towards deconstructing the hierarchies that have caused harm ... We strive to cultivate a balanced offering of voices, and aim to welcome a wider range of participants by greatly expanding our scholarship programs.

voices.text: Applications ARE currently closed. New cohort date TBD.

New cohort date TBD', all dates render as 'DATE TBA' or 'DATE TBD', the homepage carousel still advertises an 'OCTOBER 2021 • LOS ANGELES, CA' cohort, and every page footer reads '© 2022 | Psychedelic Coalition for Health'. gaps: No current cohort dates, and no statement anywhere about whether the programme is on hiatus or has ended.
Two conflicting CE figures — 50 CEs on the continuing education page, 'up to 60 CE' in the site-wide footer — with no reconciliation and no breakdown of how the credits are allocated across the week.
No total contact-hour count for the training itself.
Two conflicting tuition blocks left live on the same page ($5,000/$6,000 and $4,000/$5,000/$1,500), with no indication which applies to a future cohort.

No refund or cancellation policy for the training — the published policies page covers only the Symposium.

No published screening or medical-eligibility criteria for the participant ketamine sessions, and no statement of who prescribes and supervises them on site. For a training whose core is participants taking a scheduled drug, this is the most significant omission.
No cohort size published.

No verified YouTube video about this specific training. Videos featuring Nicholas Brüss exist (e.g. a Yale Psychedelic Science Group talk on psychedelic-assisted IFS) but are about his clinical work, not about PCH, so none is included here.

soundmind-institute.name: SoundMind Psychedelic Facilitator Training Program
soundmind-institute.org: SoundMind Institute (training arm of SoundMind; affiliated with SoundMind Center, Philadelphia)
soundmind-institute.location: Online nationally, with in-person practicum hubs; DORA lists the programme at 555 Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd, Suite 105, Portland, OR 97214. Retreats and practicums have run in Colorado, Oregon, Philadelphia, Jamaica, Costa Rica and Peru.
soundmind-institute.one_line: A 12-month, mostly online facilitator training that is currently on Colorado's approved training programme list — so its Colorado track leads somewhere real — but is no longer on Oregon's, despite having been one of the first three programmes OHA approved back in 2022.
summary: SoundMind is a nonprofit-affiliated training run by Hannah C. McLane, MD, MA, MPH, who designed and teaches it. The 2026–27 cohort structure is: enrol any time between 15 March and 15 September 2026, start with a self-paced prerequisite 'Psychodynamic Techniques for Psychedelic Facilitators' course, then from September 2026 attend required live Zoom sessions on Tuesdays 7–9pm ET with guest lecturers, plus a supervised weekly accountability group (tentatively Thursdays 7–8pm ET). Expect 8–10 hours a week outside class for readings and homework. To be certified you must complete all readings, homework and quizzes, pass a written comprehensive exam, and attend the main class — five absences are allowed. There is a 'Global Access Program' for people who cannot make the live hours.

Tuition is stated only as a range, $5,800 to $10,300, 'depending on the program you choose', with the specifics reserved for a call. The 40-hour in-person practicum required for the full certificate is a further $2,500–$4,500 and is not included in tuition; you have two years after graduation to complete it. Practicums use psilocybin or ketamine depending on whether you want the Colorado psilocybin certificate. Refunds are full and no-questions-asked up to three weeks before the programme starts. Roughly 30% of past cohorts were not clinicians — SoundMind takes an explicit position that restricting training to licence-holders is itself an equity problem.

On equity, the concrete things — as distinct from the mission statement — are: the BIPOC Psychedelic Leadership Program, a free 10-month fellowship for 15 BIPOC fellows meeting monthly with five core facilitators, whose graduates SoundMind lists publicly so organisations can book them; a Psychedelics and Identity Initiative building retreat protocols and clinician materials around sexuality and gender-identity shifts that surface in sessions; a stated requirement that all teachers be 'grounded in an anti-racist, anti-oppression framework'; a Native American Outreach Coordinator (Belinda Eriacho, Diné and Zuni) who also instructs; a Peer Support Model aimed at Veterans, BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ clients; and a curriculum module, 'Ethical and Inclusive Practice', covering consent, boundaries and BIPOC access. The affiliated Philadelphia clinic is the delivery vehicle for most of this.

On neurodiversity, be more careful. There is no neurodiversity module in the published curriculum. What exists is: McLane identifies as neurodiverse (dyslexia and ADHD) and researches cognitive diversity, psychedelics and ADHD; and SoundMind's own 2023 press release lists 'Neurodiverse individuals' among the populations its equitable-care models serve. That is a founder's research interest and an organisational claim, not a taught component you can point to in the syllabus. The one structural feature that arguably supports neurodivergent students — recorded lectures, five permitted absences, a self-paced Global Access track — is framed by SoundMind as scheduling flexibility, not as accommodation.

cost.note: SoundMind publishes a range, not a price: 'The cost of the program ranges from $5,800 to $10,300, depending on the program you choose. Please schedule a call to discuss your options.' The 40-hour in-person practicum required for the full certificate costs an additional $2,500–$4,500 and is explicitly 'not included in the course tuition fee'. Colorado's post-programme 40 hours of consultation supervision is also not included. Early-bird discounts are advertised without figures. Full refund, no questions asked, up to three weeks before the start.

soundmind-institute.length: 12 months. You can start as early as 15 March 2026 and as late as 15 September 2026 to be part of the 2026–2027 cohort; required live sessions begin September 2026. The 40-hour practicum can be completed up to two years after graduation.
soundmind-institute.hours: Not published as a single total. Weekly: 2 hours of live class, 1 hour of small group, and 8–10 hours of readings and homework. Plus a required 40-hour in-person practicum for the full certificate. A 2023 SoundMind press release described an earlier version of the programme as '200-hour' over eight months; the current page does not give an hour total, so do not assume the two are the same programme.
soundmind-institute.format: Hybrid, weighted heavily online. Self-paced prerequisite psychodynamic course on the platform; required live Zoom classes Tuesdays 7–9pm ET with rotating guest lecturers; required weekly accountability groups supervised by two teaching assistants (tentatively Thursdays 7–8pm ET); self-paced video and reading modules; all classes recorded and available after the course. A 'Global Access Program' offers a more self-paced route for people who cannot attend live. The in-person element is a 40-hour practicum, offered by SoundMind and affiliated partners through the year, using psilocybin or ketamine; on some practicums students may receive treatment from another student, but this is not required to graduate.
soundmind-institute.eligibility: Deliberately open. 'We open the application to everyone who is interested in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy facilitation. About 30% of students in previous cohorts were not clinicians yet.' SoundMind states its position directly: 'We have always believed that an equitable and thriving psychedelic ecosystem is not one that limits training programs to those with pre-existing medical or mental health licensure.' It prioritises applicants with experience of non-ordinary states, a daily meditation practice, curiosity about the scientific literature, and skills such as bodywork, somatic training or herbalism. Applicants with no psychotherapy or clinical background may still apply and, if accepted, receive preparation homework. Process: apply, then a live interview with the team. A California LMFT is comfortably eligible; so is a member of the public, which is worth knowing about your future cohort.

curriculum.detail: The research on ketamine, psilocybin and MDMA; psychodynamic skills tailored for psychedelic therapy; cultural, legal and ethical considerations.
Ketamine's use in depression, PTSD and anxiety; guiding clients from preparation through integration; supervised ketamine sessions for practical experience.
Guiding clients through psilocybin therapy; immersive retreats in Colorado; 'Meet State Standards: Fulfill all requirements for certification to practice in Colorado.'
Meeting your own thoughts and emotions; developing a personal meditation practice; training in leading others through guided meditation.
Techniques to help clients integrate experiences into daily life; tools supporting reflection, self-awareness and actionable steps.
Clinical ethics and boundaries — consent, patient care, professional boundaries; cultural sensitivity and inclusion, 'ensuring healing spaces are inclusive for BIPOC and marginalized communities'.
Ceremonial and historical traditions informing psychedelic healing; their origins; applying culturally respectful and ethical practices; honouring traditions while adapting them responsibly.
Somatic techniques for processing emotion and trauma through the body; the link between physical sensation and emotional healing; breathwork, grounding exercises, mindful movement.
Recognising and addressing trauma responses during psychedelic sessions; creating a safe and supportive environment; managing difficult experiences.
Recently added self-paced prerequisite curriculum giving all students a foundation in psychoanalytic and psychodynamic therapy skills before the live course begins.

can: Keep practising as a California LMFT with a certificate from a school. It confers nothing on your BBS licence; the BBS neither issues nor recognises a psychedelic-therapy credential.

Take the Colorado track and, on completion, pursue Colorado natural medicine facilitator licensure. This one is real and checkable: 'SoundMind Institute Psychedelic Facilitator Training Program' appears on DORA's Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs list, with Didactic, Practicum and Consultation all marked Yes (checked 6 August 2026). SoundMind states you will still need 40 hours of consultation supervision after the programme, at your own cost, to get a full licence.

Practise ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in California in collaboration with a prescriber — the training teaches you to hold space, prepare and integrate. SoundMind is unusually direct about the division of labour: 'To provide ketamine-assisted therapy, a facilitator must be affiliated with a physician who can prescribe ketamine.'
Do preparation and integration work, which needs no credential at all, and which SoundMind explicitly emphasises as a track in its own right.
Have supervised hands-on experience with psilocybin or ketamine via the 40-hour practicum, in a jurisdiction where that is legal.
Enter the field without a clinical licence, if that describes you — this is one of the few programmes that says so openly rather than quietly.
cannot: Give you any legal ability in California beyond what your LMFT licence already provides. Psilocybin and MDMA remain Schedule I federally and there is no California therapeutic framework: SB 58 was vetoed in October 2023, and California's 2025 legislative action was a bill to accelerate the study of psychedelics for PTSD, not to legalise therapeutic use.

Get you an Oregon psilocybin facilitator licence. SoundMind was approved by OHA in June 2022 and announced it as being 'one of the first three programs in the world' — but it does not appear on OHA's current live list of training programmes with approved curriculum (15 programmes, checked 6 August 2026). The programme's own 2026 page now markets state approval only for Colorado. If Oregon is your goal, this is the wrong programme unless SoundMind can show you a current OHA approval and HECC licensure in writing.
Prescribe or administer anything. Their own disclaimer: this training 'does not provide the ability to prescribe ketamine, psilocybin or administer them without proper medical licensure.'

Be presented as an accreditation. SoundMind says it plainly: outside Oregon and Colorado 'there is no standardization or credentialing board for psychedelic-assisted therapy at this time, which means no individual course or program can provide "accreditation" to practice with psychedelics.'
Qualify you to practise independently on completion. 'Continued hands-on learning and ongoing clinical supervision are strongly recommended before practicing independently.'

Count toward your California BBS continuing education, as far as anything published shows. No CE or CME credit is advertised anywhere on the programme page or FAQ — unlike IPI and PCH, which both publish accredited CE arrangements. Ask before you assume.
scope.disclaimer_quote: **Important Disclaimer: This training does not provide the ability to prescribe ketamine, psilocybin or administer them without proper medical licensure. It is designed for therapeutic and facilitative roles within a collaborative care framework.
