spiral-process-training.name: Psychedelic Process Training for Therapists
spiral-process-training.location: Santa Cruz, CA — fully in person
spiral-process-training.one_line: A six-day, $1,950 in-person ketamine-and-somatics intensive in Santa Cruz run by one LMFT, where the tuition includes two ketamine sessions for you as a student.
summary: This is the smallest and cheapest of the trainings in this directory, and the most concretely about work a California therapist can legally do tomorrow. It is six days in person in Santa Cruz — two three-day weekends, 10am to 5pm, no virtual option — taught by Dmitry Vulfovich, LMFT, the founder and clinical director of Spiral Process Therapy, a Campbell/South Bay practice that offers ketamine-assisted psychotherapy. The stated content is the full arc of a psychedelic-assisted session: assessment and vetting, preparation and priming, in-session facilitation using experiential methods (movement, chair work, expressive arts, guided imagery), touch and attachment work, integration, and coordinating with the prescriber who actually writes the ketamine script.

The unusual feature is the tuition structure. $1,950 covers the training and, per the program's own page, 'includes ketamine medicine (2 sessions) for each student.' Because ketamine has to be routed through a medical prescriber, the program says refunds will not be granted except for a compelling medical emergency. A $450 deposit plus $50 processing fee is due at registration. There is no published payment-plan schedule beyond 'available per request.'

Eligibility is broad on paper and narrower in the fine print. The Psychedelic Process Training page says the course is 'open to all healing practitioners including coaches, shamans, nurses, doctors, licensed therapists and registered associates,' and that the organisation 'highly value[s]' applicants who have done its own Spiral Process Method (SPM) course or an equivalent experiential foundation such as Hakomi, IFS or Somatic Experiencing. The separate SPM course page states it more firmly: 'Completion of this course is also a prerequisite for the Psychedelic Process Training.' Those two sentences do not agree, and a prospective student should get the answer in writing before paying a non-refundable deposit. SPM itself is a separate 7-day, $1,750 course.

Continuing education is the other thing to pin down. Spiral Process Therapy is a CAMFT-approved CE sponsor (provider number 1000186) and awards 35 CE hours for the SPM course, explicitly meeting California BBS requirements for LMFT, LCSW, LPCC and LEP renewal. The Psychedelic Process Training page carries the same accommodations-and-grievances boilerplate a CE-approved course would, but states no CE hour count anywhere. Ask. Six days at roughly 6 instructional hours a day is about 36 hours of teaching, which would be meaningful CE if it is in fact approved.

cost.note: $1,950 per participant for the September 2026 cohort; the program states this 'includes ketamine medicine (2 sessions) for each student.' $450 deposit plus $50 processing fee at registration, balance due before the start date. Payment plans 'available per request' (no published terms). Refunds are not granted except for a compelling medical emergency, because of the prescriber logistics. Travel and lodging for both Santa Cruz weekends are not included and not priced. The prerequisite Spiral Process Method course, if required, is a separate $1,750 plus $300 deposit and $50 processing fee.

spiral-process-training.length: 6 days, delivered as two three-day weekends within one month (September 11-13 and 25-27, 2026)
spiral-process-training.hours: Six days at 10am-5pm including a one-hour lunch and two 15-minute breaks — roughly 5.5 instructional hours per day, about 33 hours total. The program does not publish an official hour count or a CE hour count for this course.
spiral-process-training.format: In person only, in Santa Cruz, California. 'Virtual attendance is not available – this is an in-person immersive program.' Both weekends require accommodation for out-of-town participants.
spiral-process-training.eligibility: Stated as open to 'all healing practitioners including coaches, shamans, nurses, doctors, licensed therapists and registered associates (LMFT, LCSW, MFT, psychologists, and equivalents).' The training page says the program 'highly value[s]' completion of its own Spiral Process Method course or an equivalent experiential foundation (Hakomi, IFS, Somatic Experiencing); the SPM course page states outright that SPM completion 'is also a prerequisite for the Psychedelic Process Training.' Registration deadline for the September 2026 cohort is 21 August 2026.

curriculum.module: The altered state and 'inner healing intelligence'
curriculum.detail: Understanding the altered state and its opportunity to access the inner healing intelligence.
How to assess if a client is appropriate for psychedelic treatment.
How to prepare a client for the psychedelic experience, and how to prime a client's process to help them orient for the most meaningful outcome.

Movement, somatic work, chair work, expressive arts, guided imagery and more, used to deepen the client toward their inner healing intelligence; holding space 'in a dynamic, centered and non-agendized manner.'
How to use touch and attachment healing as part of psychedelic therapy.
How to help the client integrate and apply the lessons and newfound perspectives into their daily life.
How to work with the providers, prescribers and community leaders to give clients access to the medicine — the practical piece of KAP, since the therapist does not prescribe.

can: Practise ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in California as the therapist half of a two-role arrangement — you do the preparation, sit the session and do the integration, while a physician, NP or PA evaluates the client and prescribes the ketamine. Ketamine is an FDA-approved anaesthetic prescribed off-label for psychiatric indications; nothing about this training authorises you to prescribe or dispense it.
Offer psychedelic integration therapy in California. Integration is ordinary psychotherapy about an experience the client had elsewhere, and requires no special credential beyond your BBS licence.
Use the experiential, somatic and touch-based methods taught here inside your existing scope as an LMFT, LCSW, LPCC or psychologist, subject to your board's rules on touch and informed consent.
Have had two supervised ketamine sessions yourself, which is the sort of first-hand experience clinics and KAP practices ask about when hiring.

Plausibly claim California BBS continuing education — but only if this specific course is CE-approved. Spiral Process Therapy is a CAMFT-approved CE sponsor (provider 1000186) and awards 35 CE hours for its Spiral Process Method course; the Psychedelic Process Training page states no CE hours at all. Confirm before you assume.
cannot: Change your licence or scope of practice. This is a certificate from a private practice, not a credential from the California Board of Behavioral Sciences. The BBS does not recognise, require or register psychedelic-therapy certificates.
Prescribe, administer, supply or possess ketamine. That is the prescriber's role, and it stays the prescriber's role after this course.

Legally work with psilocybin or MDMA with clients in California. Psilocybin and psilocyn are Schedule I under California Health & Safety Code §11054(d)(18)-(19), and MDMA-assisted therapy has no FDA approval — the FDA issued Lykos Therapeutics a complete response letter in August 2024 and no MDMA product is approved as of August 2026.

Qualify for the Oregon psilocybin facilitator licence or the Colorado natural medicine facilitator licence. Spiral Process Therapy does not appear on the Oregon Health Authority's list of training programs with approved curriculum, nor on Colorado DORA's list of approved Natural Medicine Training Programs (both checked 6 August 2026).
Call yourself a 'psychedelic therapist' as a protected or regulated title. No such title exists in California.

uc-berkeley-bcsp.name: Berkeley Psychedelic Facilitation Certificate Program
uc-berkeley-bcsp.org: UC Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics (BCSP), in partnership with the UC Berkeley School of Education
uc-berkeley-bcsp.location: Berkeley, CA — mostly in person, plus one residential retreat per year in Northern California
uc-berkeley-bcsp.one_line: A nine-month, $14,000, chaplaincy-flavoured facilitator training from a major public university — Oregon-approved, distinctive, and closed to new students since 2025 with no announced restart.
summary: This was, from 2022 to 2025, the only psychedelic facilitator training run inside a top-tier American public research university. UC Berkeley's Center for the Science of Psychedelics incubated it in partnership with Berkeley's School of Education; the two graduating cohorts ran nine months each, 200 hours in total, and it was built for a specific and unusual audience — 'advanced religious, spiritual care, and healthcare professionals working in areas such as chaplaincy, ministry, medicine, nursing, midwifery, mental health counseling, psychiatry, and social work', plus people trained in traditional plant-medicine lineages who carried the support of their community. The centre of gravity was spiritual care rather than clinical protocol: the nine curriculum domains put Spiritual Care, Ancestral Entheogenic Traditions, Reciprocity and Ecological Awareness and Contemplative Practice alongside Psychotherapeutic Methods and Clinical Science. That is not a marketing gloss — the programme director, Moana Meadow, is an interfaith minister and hospice chaplain, and the programme was run out of a School of Education as an explicit 'laboratory school' collecting research data on how to train facilitators.

The teaching was heavily in person, which is what made it expensive and what made alumni rate it. Of the 160 instructional hours, roughly 90% were face to face across seven modules of three to five days: five or six non-residential modules in Berkeley each year plus one residential retreat at a Northern California retreat centre, supplemented by monthly online small groups and JEDI (justice, equity, diversity, inclusion) panels. Expect another ~160 hours of reading and written work — about four to five hours a week for nine months. A further optional 40-hour practicum (30 hours of direct facilitation or observation of non-ordinary states, 10 hours of professional consultation) was what actually unlocked Oregon or Colorado licensure, and it carried an extra fee on top of tuition. Cohorts were deliberately small: 25–30 in the first two years, expanded to 60 for 2024-25.

Enrolment is paused and has been since the 2025-26 academic year. BCSP's own explanation is unusually candid: 'In response to multiple factors, including changing policies and regulatory requirements at the campus, state, and federal levels; decreased demand for facilitation training; and decreased philanthropic support for University-based psychedelic education, enrollment is paused for 2025-2026.' The programme became administratively independent from BCSP on 1 July 2025 and moved wholly into the School of Education; the BCSP pages are now a frozen archive that says so at the top of every page. Staff say they will spend the pause analysing and publishing four years of programme data, held a first alumni gathering in September 2025, and 'will also consider formats for continuing education' — but no restart date, no new site, and no new tuition figure has been published as of 6 August 2026.

The credential still does something, which is why it is worth understanding even paused. The certificate was an Oregon Health Authority approved Psilocybin Facilitator Training Program (ID #TP-b174a696), approved through Oregon's Higher Education Coordinating Commission 'until 2027', and Oregon's live approved-curriculum list still carried 'Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics - Psychedelic Facilitation Certificate Program' when checked on 6 August 2026. Holders of a 2023-2025 Certificate of Completion remain eligible to pursue Oregon licensure, and Colorado licensure on top of that with supplemental training and practicum hours. None of that changes anything about practising in California. BCSP's other public offerings are still open and are education, not training: the free-to-audit online course 'Psychedelics and the Mind' with Professor David Presti (8 modules, 8+ hours of video, $85 for the verified certificate track, reduced from $135), plus The Microdose newsletter, the Altered States podcast, a state-by-state Law and Policy Map, a clinical trials map and a patent tracker.
modality: Ancestral/traditional entheogens covered contextually (ayahuasca, huachuma, peyote, iboga) but not taught as techniques

cost.note: Final published standard enrolment fee was $14,000, covering the 160 instructional hours only — not travel, accommodation, books, or the fees for the required 40 practicum hours. Across the programme's three years the FAQ describes standard fees of $10,000-$14,000. Application fee $175 (waivable). JEDI and need-based scholarships were donor-funded: in 2022-23 and 2023-24, 100% of qualified applicants requesting aid received it, representing 30% of enrolment fees; in 2024-25 that fell to 20% of enrolment fees. No tuition figure exists for any future cohort.

uc-berkeley-bcsp.hours: 200 hours: 160 instructional (about 90% in person) across seven three- to five-day modules, plus monthly online small groups and JEDI panels; plus an optional 40-hour practicum (30 hours direct facilitation/observation of non-ordinary states + 10 hours professional consultation) required only for Oregon or Colorado licensure. Roughly a further 160 hours of reading and assignments (4-5 hours a week).
uc-berkeley-bcsp.format: Primarily in person in Berkeley — five to six non-residential modules a year plus one residential retreat a year at a Northern California retreat centre — complemented by asynchronous and online small-group learning. Most modules ran Friday and Saturday 9:00am-5:00pm and Sunday 9:00am-3:30pm. Cohorts of 24-60 (capped at 25-30 in years one and two, expanded to 60 in year three).
uc-berkeley-bcsp.eligibility: Closed. When open: advanced religious, spiritual care and healthcare professionals — chaplaincy, ministry, medicine, nursing, midwifery, mental health counselling, psychiatry, social work — plus people trained in traditional plant-medicine lineages carrying community support. Religious professionals needed board chaplaincy certification (BCCI), one or more units of CPE, or comparable spiritual-care experience. Healthcare professionals needed a professional degree and an active licence or registration; a bachelor's degree plus at least ten years of clinical experience was also accepted, as were experienced licensed midwives. In general, trainees were licensed or certified and had at least five years of direct spiritual, mental or behavioural healthcare experience. A $175 application fee and an interview were required.

curriculum.detail: Developed and taught by programme director Moana Meadow (MA, MDiv, interfaith minister, hospice chaplain) across all three years; addressed a range of orientations to spiritual faith and practice, including Indigenous perspectives.

Directed 2022-2025 by Joseph Zamaria, PsyD, ABPP, board-certified clinical psychologist and associate clinical professor of psychiatry at UCSF, a therapist and researcher in psychedelic clinical trials.

Led 2022-2025 by Susana Bustos, PhD, a psychotherapist and music therapist and Holotropic Breathwork practitioner since 1999; framed as bridging anthropocentric healing systems with those based on human relationship to other sentiences in nature. Guest instructors included Dr Susana Bustos, Ariel Clark and Joe Tafur.
Directed 2023-2025 by Sylvestre (Sylver) Quevedo, MD, MPH, associate professor of medicine and psychiatry at UCSF and a principal investigator in FDA trials of MDMA for PTSD.

Directed 2022-2024 by Mary Sanders; covered historical and current systems of oppression, collective healing through an intersectional lens, and community-oriented infrastructures. Ran alongside a JEDI mentoring programme pairing students with psychedelic professionals from marginalised backgrounds.

Taught 2024-2025 by Angella Okawa, MA (Pacifica Graduate Institute), Hakomi- and MAPS-trained, an ordained Zen monk; framed around 'liminal fluency' — working skilfully with clients across cultures, identities and ways of knowing.

Overseen and co-taught by Kristina Hunter alongside Kylea Taylor; Hunter also served as Practicum Supervisor in 2024-25 and tracked state legalisation developments with specialised expertise in Oregon's Measure 109 policy.
Directed 2023-2025 by Dr Sylver Quevedo, including perspectives from traditional lineages; ethnobotanist Kathleen Harrison also taught in this area.
One of the nine named core domains of knowledge the programme integrated and applied. The archived pages do not name a separate somatic instructor.

30 hours of direct facilitation or observation of non-ordinary states of consciousness plus 10 hours of professional consultation. Designed by each student with instructional staff support. Some placements were provided by the programme; all were optional and carried an additional cost. Required to pursue Oregon or Colorado licensure.

can: Nothing about this certificate changes a California BBS licence. A California LMFT, LCSW or LPCC holding it practises exactly the same scope they held before — psychotherapy — and the BBS neither recognises nor requires the credential.

Do preparation and integration work with California clients who obtain psychedelics elsewhere. This is ordinary psychotherapy and needs no special credential at all; the training makes you better at it, not more permitted.

Practise ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in California — the one psychedelic modality legally available to a California therapist today. Ketamine is an FDA-approved anaesthetic prescribed off-label; the therapist does not prescribe or dispense it. A physician, NP or PA does. At least two of the programme's own published alumni are California LMFTs doing exactly this.

Apply for an Oregon psilocybin facilitator licence, if you hold a 2023-2025 Certificate of Completion and completed the 40-hour practicum. The programme was an OHA-approved training programme (ID #TP-b174a696) and still appeared on Oregon's live approved-curriculum list when checked on 6 August 2026. Oregon requires you to be 21+, hold a high-school diploma, pass a criminal background check, complete an approved programme including practicum and its exams, pass the OPS regulations exam, pay a $150 application fee and then a $2,000 annual licence fee ($1,000 reduced for veterans, SSI, SNAP or Oregon Health Plan recipients). The Oregon residency requirement expired in January 2025, so a Californian can hold this licence — but must physically facilitate in a licensed Oregon service centre.

Pursue Colorado facilitator licensure on top of Oregon licensure, per BCSP: holders of a 2023-2025 certificate 'are eligible to pursue licensure in Oregon as well as Colorado (the latter requires supplemental training and practicum hours)'.

Be credible to a research team, a KAP clinic, or a future employer. The programme is small, university-badged and unusually well documented, and its faculty roster (UCSF, MAPS/Lykos-adjacent, Paul Stamets as a guest lecturer) travels.
cannot: Administer psilocybin or MDMA to anyone in California. Both remain Schedule I federally, and California has no regulated access programme — SB 58 was vetoed by Governor Newsom in October 2023, and the 2025-26 California bills (AB 1103, SB 751, SB 1224, AB 2489) are research-funding and study measures, not access frameworks.
Enrol. Enrolment has been paused since the 2025-26 academic year and no restart has been announced. The BCSP pages are an archive and stop being updated on 1 July 2025.

Use it as a Colorado training credential on its own. BCSP does not appear on Colorado DORA's list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs (checked 6 August 2026), so it does not by itself satisfy Colorado's 150-hour didactic requirement — Colorado is reachable via the Oregon route or with supplemental training.
Bill insurance for anything, prescribe anything, or supervise anyone in a psychedelic capacity in California.

Claim to be a 'certified psychedelic therapist' in any regulated sense. The programme's own FAQ is explicit that graduates were not licensed, certified or sanctioned to work where regulations did not permit it.
scope.disclaimer_quote: Trainees who completed the program were not licensed, certified, or otherwise sanctioned to provide psychedelic care in settings where regulations did not permit psychedelic work.

faculty: Moana Meadow, MA, MDiv — Program Staff Director since 2022 and author of the spiritual care curriculum. Interfaith minister ordained at the Chaplaincy Institute, hospice chaplain, birth doula, former executive director of a plant-medicine church, advisory board of the Sacred Plant Alliance. She is the reason this programme reads differently from every clinical-protocol training.

Guest lecturers included mycologist Paul Stamets, Dr Pam Kryskow, Dr Gregory Cajete (Santa Clara Pueblo educator), and psychiatric NP Andrew Penn.

vital-psychedelics-today.name: Vital — Certificate in Integrative Psychedelic Studies
vital-psychedelics-today.location: Fully online — “All classes are 100% digital, requiring no travel”
vital-psychedelics-today.one_line: A $10,500, 12-month, entirely remote psychedelic education programme from the Psychedelics Today podcast company that requires no clinical degree, awards a certificate with no legal force, and — for a licensed California therapist — is worth buying mainly for up to 68 BBS-countable CE credits and the network.
summary: Vital is the flagship training of Psychedelics Today, the podcast and media company run by Joe Moore and Kyle Buller. It is a 12-month, fully remote programme delivered as a weekly two-hour live lecture with Q&A plus a weekly 90-minute small-group study session, wrapped in a private online community, recorded lecture archive, biweekly office hours and optional discussion groups. Graduates receive a “Certificate in Integrative Psychedelic Studies,” optionally with a specialisation in one of five named tracks: Regenerative Business & Leadership, Depth & Jungian Perspectives, Somatics & Trauma, Spiritual Emergence, or Microdosing. To graduate you must attend at least 80% of study groups, complete a foundational essay and a final project, and complete an experiential elective.

It is not a clinical training and it does not pretend to be. “No specific licenses or prerequisites are required,” the admissions FAQ says; “the program is not limited to licensed mental health professionals or practitioners already seeing clients.” The room is therefore mixed — clinicians, coaches, wellness practitioners, entrepreneurs, researchers, policy people. The faculty list is genuinely strong for a media company: Bill Richards (Johns Hopkins, Sunstone Therapies), Sara Reed, Casey Paleos, MD (a Phase 3 MDMA principal investigator), Devon Christie, MD, Ben Malcolm, PharmD, Charles Nichols, PhD, ethics author Kylea Taylor, LMFT, and drug-policy attorney Courtney Barnes, JD. Note the site's own caveat: “Presenters and Core Study Group Instructors are subject to change. This list is based on previous cohorts.”

Cost is $10,500, with a $2,000 early-bird discount for payment by 7 August 2026, payment plans via Affirm and Afterpay, and a non-refundable payment due within two weeks of acceptance. A business-focused mentorship add-on runs another $2,000. Time commitment as published is “at least 3.5 hours per week in live classes and study groups, plus an additional 2 hours per week on supplementary materials.” Vital states students “may be eligible for up to 68 Continuing Education (CE) credits upon completion, pending approval,” provided by the Spiritual Competency Academy. That matters concretely for a California LMFT: SCA is an APA-approved CE sponsor, and the California Board of Behavioral Sciences accepts APA-approved CE for MFT, LCSW and LPCC renewal. Verify the “pending approval” status for your cohort before you pay.

Two figures widely repeated about Vital in directories are out of date and should not be relied on. The “roughly 180 hours” and “$12,000” numbers, and the mandatory in-person residential retreat, come from the 2022 first cohort's marketing page, which advertised “180 hours of live teaching, experience, and practice,” tuition of $12,000, six retreat options and a “Certificate in Psychedelic Therapies and Integration.” The current programme publishes no total hour count, costs $10,500, is 100% digital, and awards a differently named certificate. The experiential elective is still required but the FAQ states travel is not: “Some students opt to travel to fulfill this requirement, but it is not mandatory.” Psychedelics Today says over 400 students went through the first three cohorts.

cost.note: $10,500 total tuition for the October 2026 cohort. $2,000 early-bird discount for payment by 7 August 2026. A non-refundable payment is due within two weeks of acceptance. Payment plans via Affirm and Afterpay; regional taxes may apply. Optional mentorship add-on is a further $2,000. Summer elective courses are $99 each unless you are in the mentorship track. Cost of the required experiential elective is not included and is not published — if you choose a retreat, that is a separate purchase.

vital-psychedelics-today.length: 12 months. The October 2026 cohort's start is published; the end date is listed as “TBD.”
vital-psychedelics-today.hours: No total hour count is published for the current programme. What is published: “at least 3.5 hours per week in live classes and study groups, plus an additional 2 hours per week on supplementary materials” — i.e. a weekly 2-hour live lecture and a weekly 90-minute study group, roughly 5.5 hours a week across 12 months. Up to 68 CE credits, pending approval, via the Spiritual Competency Academy. The frequently cited “180 hours” figure is from Vital's 2022 launch page and does not appear anywhere on the current site.
vital-psychedelics-today.format: Entirely remote and largely synchronous: weekly live 2-hour lecture plus Q&A, weekly 90-minute faculty-led small-group study session, all lectures recorded, online community platform, biweekly staff office hours, optional biweekly “Vital Elements” discussion groups. Assessment is a foundational essay plus a final project, with a minimum 80% study-group attendance requirement. A required experiential elective can be fulfilled without travel.
vital-psychedelics-today.eligibility: Open to anyone. “No license or prerequisites are required.” Vital states the programme “is not limited to licensed mental health professionals or practitioners already seeing clients,” and prior psychedelic experience is not mandatory though “some experience with non-ordinary states of consciousness and previous education on psychedelics are encouraged.” Applications for the October 2026 cohort were due 13 September, reviewed on a rolling basis with preference to early applicants.

curriculum.detail: “2-hour lectures and Q&A sessions” each week with a guest expert; may be delivered live or as a pre-recorded class. All are recorded and available for later review.
“Weekly 90-minute sessions in small groups” led by a core study-group instructor. Attendance at at least 80% is required to graduate.
“Deepen self-awareness and demonstrate understanding.” These are the graduation requirements alongside study-group attendance.
“To amplify your transformation through personal experience.” Required for completion, but students choose the form and travel is not mandatory. Vital does not provide or supply any substance.

Monthly group Zoom sessions plus three one-to-one sessions with a core Vital team member, aimed at “business leaders, founders, entrepreneurs, clinic owners, supervisors and community leaders.” Business development, not clinical supervision.

can: IF YOU ARE A LICENSED CALIFORNIA LMFT: earn up to 68 continuing education credits (Vital says “pending approval”) issued by the Spiritual Competency Academy. SCA is an APA-approved CE sponsor and the California Board of Behavioral Sciences accepts APA-approved CE for LMFT, LCSW and LPCC renewal — so this is the one part of the $10,500 with a concrete regulatory use. Confirm the approval is in place for your cohort in writing before paying.

IF YOU ARE A LICENSED LMFT: do psychedelic integration and preparation work with clients. That is already inside your licensed scope; Vital gives you a framework and a peer group for it, not permission.

IF YOU ARE A LICENSED LMFT: work as the therapist on a ketamine-assisted psychotherapy team, since ketamine is Schedule III and prescribed off-label by a physician, NP or PA. Note Vital is substance-agnostic education, not a KAP clinical protocol training — if KAP practice is your goal, this is not the most direct purchase.

IF YOU ARE NOT LICENSED: work in the parts of the field that require no licence — psychedelic education, harm reduction, research coordination, policy and advocacy, writing, running a clinic or retreat business, product and community work. Vital's own materials point squarely at these roles, and its “Emerging Psychedelic Workforce” report surveyed 130 students and graduates about exactly this.

IF YOU ARE NOT LICENSED: work as a coach. Coaching is not a licensed profession in California — but see the “cannot” list, because the line between coaching and psychotherapy is where unlicensed practitioners get into legal trouble, not a grey area you can talk your way across.
Anyone: access a substantial faculty and a large alumni network. Over 400 students went through the first three cohorts; some became Vital instructors.
cannot: The certificate confers no legal authority of any kind. Vital states it twice, plainly: “*Vital certificate does not grant any legal authorizations regarding psychedelic use,” and “No, this certificate does not grant any new legal authorizations regarding psychedelic use. It expands your competence and confidence but does not grant legal qualifications or vocational accreditations.”

IF YOU ARE NOT LICENSED: you cannot practise psychotherapy in California, full stop. Business and Professions Code § 4980(b): “A person shall not engage in the practice of marriage and family therapy… unless the person holds a valid license.” BPC § 2903(a) separately bars unlicensed practice of psychology, and defines psychotherapy as “the use of psychological methods in a professional relationship to assist a person… to modify feelings, conditions, attitudes, and behaviors.” Running integration sessions that assess, diagnose or treat psychological distress for a fee is practising psychotherapy regardless of what you call the invoice.

IF YOU ARE NOT LICENSED: you cannot call yourself a therapist, counsellor, psychotherapist, LMFT/MFT/MFCC, or psychologist, or imply licensure. BPC § 4980(d)(2) prohibits using those letters or “another name, word, initial, or symbol… to imply licensure.” “Certified in Integrative Psychedelic Studies” is not a protected title and does not substitute for one.

Nobody with this certificate can legally administer psilocybin or MDMA anywhere in the United States on its strength. Both are Schedule I (21 CFR § 1308.11(d)); California has no state-regulated psychedelic services programme as of August 2026; FDA has not approved MDMA-assisted therapy since the August 2024 complete response letter to Lykos.

It does not qualify you for Oregon psilocybin facilitator licensure. Oregon only counts training whose curriculum has been approved by Oregon Psilocybin Services under ORS 475A; Vital makes no such claim and is not structured for it.
It does not qualify you for Colorado natural medicine facilitator licensure. Vital does not appear on Colorado DORA's list of Approved Natural Medicine Training Programs (checked 6 August 2026).

It does not change the scope of practice of an already-licensed therapist by one inch. The BBS neither requires nor recognises psychedelic certificates, and there is no BBS specialty designation to earn.
scope.disclaimer_quote: No, this certificate does not grant any new legal authorizations regarding psychedelic use. It expands your competence and confidence but does not grant legal qualifications or vocational accreditations.

faculty: Bill Richards, STM, PhD — Johns Hopkins psychedelic research pioneer, author of Sacred Knowledge, now Director of Training at Sunstone Therapies. The most senior name on the list.

Sara Reed — psychedelic research therapist at Imperial College London; former study therapist on a MAPS Phase 2 MDMA trial for PTSD; works on culture and mental health.
Devon Christie, MD — Senior Lead of Psychedelic Programs at Numinus; trained in both MDMA- and ketamine-assisted psychotherapy.
Ben Malcolm, PharmD, MPH — psychiatric pharmacist (“Spirit Pharmacist”), the go-to source on psychedelic–psychiatric medication interactions.
Charles Nichols, PhD — professor of pharmacology, LSU Health Sciences Center; psychedelic pharmacology.
Kylea Taylor, MS, LMFT — creator of InnerEthics®, author of The Ethics of Caring, senior trainer in Grof Transpersonal Training. Relevant given the field's boundary-violation history.
Courtney Barnes, JD — drug policy attorney who helped draft Denver's psilocybin decriminalisation ordinance; teaches the legal material.
Kyle Buller, MS and Joe Moore — Psychedelics Today co-founders; Buller is VP of Education and Training and a core study-group instructor.
Caveat printed on the page itself: “Presenters and Core Study Group Instructors are subject to change. This list is based on previous cohorts.” Do not enrol expecting a specific named teacher.

voices.text: The programme's own FAQ answers the only question that matters, and answers it honestly: “Does this certificate mean I am legally authorized to work with psychedelics?” — “No, this certificate does not grant any new legal authorizations regarding psychedelic use. It expands your competence and confidence but does not grant legal qualifications or vocational accreditations.” Anyone spending $10,500 should read that sentence twice: you are buying education and a network, not a licence.
voices.who: Vital course overview FAQ, verified 6 August 2026

voices.text: Cautionary precedent for the whole category. When Synthesis Institute — a comparably priced, comparably unaccredited psychedelic training company — collapsed in 2023, roughly 230 students across four cohorts of a $12,997 programme were left mid-course, with company liabilities near $850,000 and refunds contingent on a payment processor's solvency. “The greatest risk we face is if every student requests a refund this week,” the acquiring company's CEO told students. Vital requires a non-refundable payment within two weeks of acceptance for a 12-month programme whose end date it lists as “TBD.”
voices.who: Psychedelic Alpha, “Inside Synthesis Institute’s Implosion,” March 2023

voices.text: The CE claim is the strongest concrete value here, and it checks out at the provider end: “California Board of Behavioral Sciences accepts CE credits for license renewal by LCSWs, MFTs, LPCCs, and LMHCs for courses CE-approved by the American Psychological Association,” and the Spiritual Competency Academy is an APA-approved sponsor. The weak word is Vital's own: the 68 credits are “pending approval.” Get the approval confirmed in writing for your specific cohort before you pay.
voices.who: Spiritual Competency Academy CE information page, verified 6 August 2026

voices.text: Vital's public marketing has real currency problems that are worth noticing before you wire $10,500. In August 2026 the “clinicians” and “emergents” landing pages still read “APPLICATIONS NOW OPEN FOR OUR FEBRUARY 2025 COHORT” and “Cohort Launches February 17th”; the specialisations link in the site footer returns a 404; the testimonials page carries Squarespace placeholder copy (“It all begins with an idea. Maybe you want to launch a business.”) beside two named alumni; and one clinician testimonial is attributed to a “Dr. Rachel Martinez” who appears nowhere else. Meanwhile psychedelicstoday.com's banner advertises a start of “September 17” while the Vital site says October 2026.
voices.who: Direct inspection of vitalpsychedelictraining.com, 6 August 2026

voices.text: The “180 hours” figure that circulates in directories is a 2022 artefact. The original Vital page advertised “180 hours of live teaching, experience, and practice,” $12,000 tuition, a mandatory residential retreat chosen from six options, and a “Certificate in Psychedelic Therapies and Integration.” The current programme is $10,500, 100% digital with no travel requirement, publishes no total hour count, and awards a “Certificate in Integrative Psychedelic Studies.” If a directory quotes you 180 hours and a retreat, it is quoting a four-year-old page.

voices.text: “The Vital Training has not only given me a good base of theoretical knowledge but also the possibility to connect with an incredible group of folks doing amazing work in the psychedelic ecosystem.” Positive, and consistent with what the programme is — a curriculum plus a network. It is also a testimonial Psychedelics Today selected and published on its own site; no independent review platform carried usable Vital reviews that could be verified.

No refund policy is published beyond “a non-refundable payment is required within two weeks of acceptance” — the size of that non-refundable payment is not stated, nor is there any published tuition-protection arrangement.
No graduation rate, completion rate, or independent outcome data. The only workforce data is Psychedelics Today's own survey of its own students.

No independent reviews could be verified: Reddit is blocked from this environment (403), Trustpilot returned a bot-verification wall, and no journalism specifically covering Vital was found. Every named positive account traces back to Vital's own pages.

Whether Vital is on Oregon's OHA approved-curriculum list could not be confirmed by reading the list itself — OHA now serves it through a JavaScript application. The “no” rests on Vital making no such claim and on the programme having no Oregon practicum structure.
